papers.title: Measles-like hypermutation of a Newcastle disease virus drives fatal encephalitis during BCMA × CD3 T-cell-redirecting immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Abstract Newcastle disease virus (NDV or AOaV-1) is an avian paramyxovirus that typically causes only mild, self-limiting disease in humans. Here, we report fatal neuroinvasive AOaV-1 infection in a patient with multiple myeloma receiving maintenance therapy with teclistamab, daratumumab, and lenalidomide following frontline teclistamab-based treatment and autologous stem cell transplantation. Following rapidly progressive brainstem–cerebellar encephalitis and negative conventional microbiological testing, unbiased metagenomic RNA sequencing of a cerebellar biopsy identified AOaV-1 at high intraparenchymal abundance. Viral genome analysis revealed striking A-to-G and U-to-C substitutions selectively concentrated in the matrix gene, consistent with ADAR-mediated RNA editing. Long-read sequencing resolved two genetically distinct, independently hypermutated CNS haplotypes. Post-mortem analysis demonstrated widespread dissemination and continued viral diversification in multiple brain regions, whereas a peripheral urine sample contained a minimally mutated putative ancestral lineage. These findings support peripheral infection followed by CNS seeding and compartmentalized within-host evolution. The selective matrix-gene hypermutation closely parallels persistent measles virus infection in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, revealing a shared mechanism of paramyxovirus adaptation to the CNS. Profound immunotherapy-associated immune dysfunction may thus create niches enabling normally low-pathogenic zoonotic viruses to persist, evolve, and acquire severe neurovirulence.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a fatal encephalitis caused by a Newcastle disease virus (NDV) in a patient with multiple myeloma undergoing immunotherapy. The study highlights the potential for normally low-pathogenic zoonotic viruses to acquire severe neurovirulence through immune dysfunction. Using metagenomic RNA sequencing and long-read sequencing, the researchers identified hypermutated viral genomes in the central nervous system (CNS) and a minimally mutated lineage in peripheral tissues. The findings suggest that immune suppression during treatment may allow zoonotic viruses to persist, evolve, and cause severe neurological disease, similar to measles virus in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. The study's limitations include its single-case design and reliance on post-mortem analysis, which may not capture the full in vivo dynamics. The evidence supports a mechanism of paramyxovirus adaptation to the CNS, with implications for understanding viral evolution in immunocompromised hosts.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 新城疫病毒(NDV 或 AOaV-1)是一种禽副粘病毒,通常仅引起人类轻微的自限性疾病。在这里,我们报告了一名多发性骨髓瘤患者在接受基于 teclistamab 的一线 治疗 和自体干细胞移植后接受 teclistamab、达雷妥尤单抗和来那度胺维持治疗的致命性神经侵袭性 AOaV-1 感染。在快速进展的脑干-小脑脑炎和常规微生物检测阴性后,小脑活检的无偏宏基因组 RNA 测序鉴定出脑实质内高丰度的 AOaV-1。病毒 基因组 分析显示,显着的 A 至 G 和 U 至 C 取代选择性集中在基质基因中,与 ADAR 介导的 RNA 编辑一致。长读长测序解析了两种遗传上不同、独立超突变的 CNS 单倍型。尸检分析表明,病毒在多个大脑区域广泛传播和持续多样化,而外周尿液样本中含有最低限度突变的假定祖先谱系。这些发现支持外周感染,随后是 CNS 播种并在 宿主 进化 内划分。选择性基质基因超突变与 亚急性硬化性全脑炎 中的持续 麻疹病毒 感染密切相关,揭示了副粘病毒适应 CNS 的共同机制。因此,与免疫治疗相关的严重免疫功能障碍可能会创造一个生态位,使通常低致病性的人畜共患病毒能够持续存在、进化并获得严重的神经毒力。

papers.title: Phylogeography and transmission dynamics of the 2025-2026 Utah-Arizona measles outbreak: a retrospective genomic epidemiology study
papers.abstract: Background: Measles outbreaks are increasing in frequency globally as vaccine coverage decreases. During the 2025-26 Utah-Arizona border outbreak, identifying where and between whom transmission occurred was essential for directing control measures. However, epidemiological data alone are not sufficient to infer transmission patterns. Methods: As part of the local and state-wide outbreak investigation, we conducted amplicon-based whole genome sequencing on residual diagnostic samples from confirmed measles cases collected from June 15, 2025-April 30, 2026. We reconstructed viral dispersal across Utah using Bayesian phylogeographic analyses. We evaluated genetic distance thresholds for identifying recent transmission by comparing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based genetic clusters with known epidemiologic linkages. We then assessed pairwise exposures associated with genetically supported transmission linkage using logistic regression, accounting for network and spatial dependence between pairs. Findings: We generated 509 high-quality whole measles virus genomes from 913 patients. In 2025, most viral dispersal events (67.9%) originated in Southwest Utah and Mohave County, Arizona, where the first cases were reported. By 2026, most viral spread (60.5%) occurred outside of this area. A threshold of 0 SNPs identified epidemiologically linked pairs of individuals with a sensitivity of 77.4% and specificity of 92.3%. Household membership (odds ratio (OR): 219.10, 95% credible interval (CI): 112.66-325.53), participation in the same sport (OR: 15.19, 95% CI: 9.75-20.63), and attendance at the same school (OR: 51.5, 95% CI: 36.38-66.61) were independently associated with transmission linkage. Increasing distance between households was associated with reduced odds of linkage (OR: 0.46: 95% CI 0.44-0.48). Interpretation: Repeated introductions of measles virus from southwestern Utah seeded transmission elsewhere in Utah, with household, school, and sports exposures contributing to onward transmission. Validated genome-based linkage measures can complement contact tracing by helping public health teams identify likely transmission networks and prioritize investigation when resources are constrained.

papers.title: Vaccination status and its association with complications among the patients admitted with measles in the dedicated measles hospitals, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Bangladesh is facing a major resurgence of measles, with more than 60,000 suspected cases and over 600 deaths reported between March and May 2026. Despite the growing outbreak, hospital-based evidence in Bangladesh remains limited regarding measles vaccination status and its association with clinical complications. To address this critical gap, our study aimed to assess the vaccination status and its relationship with the development of clinical complications. This cross-sectional study enrolled 260 children aged 2-72 months with clinically confirmed measles who were admitted to four dedicated measles treatment hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh, between 15 and 25 April 2026. Data on vaccination status, sociodemographic characteristics, feeding practices, nutritional status, clinical symptoms, and complications were collected through caregiver interviews and hospital records. Adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated; p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Among enrolled children, 74.6% were unvaccinated, 18.8% were partially vaccinated, and only 6.5% were fully vaccinated. In the multivariable model, age below 9 months (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.03-0.268, p < 0.001) was independently associated with lower odds of vaccination, while household income at or above the median (aOR 3.983, 95% CI 1.8-8.813, p = 0.004) was associated with higher odds. Complications developed in 31.1% of cases, with respiratory involvement being most common. Absence of exclusive breastfeeding (aOR 2.336, 95% CI 1.027-5.313, p = 0.043) and presenting with exactly three symptoms at admission (aOR 3.106, 95% CI 1.274-7.572, p = 0.013) were independently associated with complications. Unvaccinated children had markedly higher odds of complications than vaccinated children (aOR 5.729, 95% CI: 2.363-13.889, p < 0.001). The heavy burden of measles among unvaccinated children, shaped by socioeconomic disadvantage and suboptimal feeding practices, underscores the urgent need to restore immunization coverage and strengthen equitable health services in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Acceptability and feasibility of measles vaccination, small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplementation, and their co-delivery among children aged 6–23 months in northern Nigeria: a qualitative study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Undernutrition and infectious diseases form a vicious cycle that endangers child survival in low-resource settings, including in Northern Nigeria. The NutriVax-Measles trial was designed to evaluate a strategy combining preventive small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) distributions with community mobilization and routine immunization services for children aged 6-23 months to improve measles vaccination uptake. To inform future programs co-delivering nutrition supplementation and immunization services at scale, we aimed to assess the feasibility and acceptability of measles vaccination, SQ-LNS distribution, and the NutriVax strategy. Methods A qualitative study was conducted at the end of the trial using in-depth interviews (n=53) and focus group discussions (n=8) with key stakeholders: caregivers, health care workers, community health workers, and community representatives. Thematic analysis was guided by multiple conceptual frameworks. Results The majority of the participants expressed satisfaction with measles vaccines in both arms, and with SQ-LNS in the NutriVax arm, as they perceived the benefits for their children’s health. In both arms, community awareness sessions and previous experience of outbreaks were key to motivating caregivers to bring their children to healthcare centres. Although distance to health facilities was identified as one of the main barriers to accessing care, SQ-LNS was perceived as an important source of motivation to bring their child to the clinic where they subsequently received vaccination. All stakeholder groups emphasized the importance of community leaders’ support and targeted male sensitization to address the prevailing sociocultural norms. Additionally, improved service organization to reduce waiting time was considered crucial to enhance caregivers’ acceptability of the intervention. Conclusion Both measles vaccination and SQ-LNS provision were acceptable and feasible, supporting the NutriVax strategy within primary healthcare settings in fragile health systems. Successful implementation depends on sustained community sensitization, continued engagement of fathers and community leaders, and service delivery decentralized as close as possible to beneficiaries. KEY MESSAGES What is already known? Co-delivering small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) with routine immunization is an effective strategy to improve vaccination coverage in Northern Nigeria. Yet, evidence on how vaccination and SQ-LNS are perceived, implemented, and experienced by stakeholders at health-care and community levels remains scarce. What are the new findings? SQ-LNS was an important source of motivation for caregivers to bring their children to health facilities, creating opportunities for vaccination. Persistent barriers to vaccination included socio-cultural misconceptions, gender norms, long waiting time and distance to health facilities. What do the new findings imply? Sustained community engagement, including targeted male sensitization, is important to improve measles vaccination acceptability. Successful implementation of co-delivery programs also requires well-organized service delivery, with services decentralized to health facilities as close as possible to beneficiaries, particularly to reduce travel distances and waiting times.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 营养不良和传染病形成恶性循环,危及资源匮乏地区(包括尼日利亚北部)的儿童生存。NutriVax-麻疹 试验旨在评估一项策略,该策略将预防性小量脂质营养补充剂 (SQ-LNS) 分发与社区动员和针对 6-23 个月儿童的常规免疫服务相结合,以提高 麻疹 疫苗接种 的吸收。为了为未来大规模共同提供营养补充和免疫服务的计划提供信息,我们旨在评估 麻疹 疫苗接种、SQ-LNS 分配和 NutriVax 策略的可行性和可接受性。方法 在试验结束时进行了一项定性研究,采用深入访谈 (n=53) 和焦点小组讨论 (n=8) 的方式与主要利益相关者:护理人员、卫生保健工作者、社区卫生工作者和社区代表进行讨论。主题分析以多个概念框架为指导。结果 大多数参与者对双臂中的 麻疹 疫苗 以及 NutriVax 臂中的 SQ-LNS 表示满意,因为他们认为这对孩子的健康有益。在这两个方面,社区意识会议和 暴发 的先前经验是激励护理人员将孩子带到医疗中心的关键。尽管距医疗机构的距离被认为是获得护理的主要障碍之一,但 SQ-LNS 被认为是带孩子去诊所接受 疫苗接种 治疗的重要动机来源。所有利益相关者团体都强调了社区领袖的支持和有针对性的男性宣传对于解决现行社会文化规范的重要性。此外,改进服务组织以减少等待时间被认为对于提高护理人员对干预措施的可接受性至关重要。结论 麻疹 疫苗接种 和 SQ-LNS 的规定都是可接受且可行的,支持脆弱卫生系统初级医疗机构中的 NutriVax 策略。成功的实施取决于持续的社区宣传、父亲和社区领袖的持续参与以及尽可能将服务交付分散到受益人身边。关键信息 什么是已知的?与常规免疫接种共同提供小量脂质营养补充剂 (SQ-LNS) 是提高尼日利亚北部 疫苗接种 覆盖率的有效策略。然而,关于医疗保健和社区层面的利益相关者如何感知、实施和体验 疫苗接种 和 SQ-LNS 的证据仍然很少。有哪些新发现? SQ-LNS 是护理人员带孩子去医疗机构就诊的重要动力来源,为 疫苗接种 创造了机会。疫苗接种 的持续障碍包括社会文化误解、性别规范、漫长的等待时间以及距医疗机构的距离。新发现意味着什么?持续的社区参与,包括有针对性的男性宣传,对于提高 麻疹 疫苗接种 的可接受性非常重要。成功实施共同交付计划还需要组织良好的服务交付,将服务分散到尽可能靠近受益人的卫生机构,特别是为了减少出行距离和等待时间。

papers.title: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh in 2026: national surveillance trends, cumulative divisional burden, and historical vaccination context
papers.abstract: Background Bangladesh experienced a major measles resurgence in 2026. We reassessed early outbreak indicators while distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden and historical vaccination measures. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) bulletins dated 2–30 April 2026, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. We reconstructed cumulative division-level counts from the 22 April bulletin and calculated population-standardized notification rates using the 2022 census. Official national measles-containing vaccine coverage for 2019, 2023 and 2024 provided historical context. Results By 30 April, DGHS reported 37,131 suspected and 5,028 confirmed cases, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. On 22 April, cumulative division-level totals were 27,164 suspected and 3,934 confirmed cases. Dhaka recorded 2,634 confirmed cases, or 5.957 per 100,000 population. Official national MCV1 and MCV2 coverage in 2024 was 86.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Earlier childhood MR1 division-level measurements were not contemporaneous with the outbreak and were not used for correlation testing. Conclusions The early outbreak showed substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity. Accurate interpretation requires matching reporting windows, strengthening age- and vaccination-status surveillance and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the measles resurgence in Bangladesh during 2026, focusing on the national surveillance trends, cumulative divisional burden, and historical vaccination context. The research aimed to reassess early outbreak indicators by distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden, and historical vaccination measures. A descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services bulletins from 2–30 April 2026 was conducted, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. By 30 April, 37,131 suspected and 5,028 confirmed measles cases were reported, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. The study highlights the substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity of the early outbreak. The findings emphasize the need for accurate interpretation by aligning reporting windows, enhancing age- and vaccination-status surveillance, and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage. The study's limitations include the lack of contemporaneous MR1 measurements for correlation testing, which affects the strength of the evidence.

papers.title: Susceptibility-weighted imaging findings in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: subcortical paramagnetic rim and deep gray matter changes.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration. With this study we aim to evaluate SWI changes in SSPE, with emphasis on the Subcortical Paramagnetic Rim (SPR) and deep gray matter mineralization, and to assess their association with parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI. T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods. RESULTS: SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: SPR and deep gray matter mineralization, are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI.
analysis_en.methods: T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods.
analysis_en.main_results: SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: SPR and deep gray matter mineralization are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions. They may inform the development of more accurate imaging-based diagnostic and staging tools for SSPE.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single-center cohort, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the reliance on semi-quantitative visual grading systems.

papers.title_zh: 亚急性硬化性全脑炎 中的磁敏感加权成像结果:皮层下顺磁边缘和深部灰质变化。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration. With this study we aim to evaluate SWI changes in SSPE, with emphasis on the Subcortical Paramagnetic Rim (SPR) and deep gray matter mineralization, and to assess their association with parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI. T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods. RESULTS: SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: SPR and deep gray matter mineralization, are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:亚急性硬化性全脑炎 (SSPE) 是一种由持续 麻疹病毒 感染引起的进行性神经退行性疾病。常规MRI在诊断和分期中起着关键作用;然而,SSPE 的磁敏加权成像 (SWI) 结果尚未得到系统表征,特别是其与疾病负担和神经退行性变的关系。通过这项研究,我们旨在评估 SSPE 中的 SWI 变化,重点关注皮质下顺磁环 (SPR) 和深部灰质矿化,并评估它们与实质疾病负担和脑萎缩的关系。方法:这项回顾性单中心研究纳入了 126 名确诊为 SSPE 的患者,这些患者接受了 MRI(包括 SWI)检查。在预先确定的幕上和幕下实质区域评估 T2/FLAIR 高信号。计算综合总实质疾病负担评分。使用半定量视觉分级系统评估脑萎缩和深层灰质矿化。还评估了 SWI 是否存在 SPR。使用非参数统计方法分析了敏感性结果、实质疾病负担、脑萎缩和临床参数之间的关联。结果:128 项 MRI 研究中有 14 项(10.9%)发现了 SPR,最常见的是顶叶。与无边缘患者相比,有边缘患者的症状持续时间明显更长、疾病分期更高、实质疾病负担更大、萎缩评分更高、深部灰质矿化评分更高(p < 0.01)。深部灰质矿化评分与整体实质疾病负担和脑萎缩呈显着正相关(Spearman's ρ,p < 0.001)。结论:SPR 和深部灰质矿化与实质疾病负担的增加和萎缩有关。这些发现可能代表了疾病慢性的影像学标志,并为传统 MRI 提供了补充信息,特别是在 麻疹 流行地区慢性脑炎的评估中。

papers.title: Clinical consultation: The role of vitamin A in the management of confirmed acute measles infection.
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, the rate of measles infection in 2026 is the highest in more than 3 decades. This clinical consultation explores the role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute measles infection and the challenges posed with this treatment in pediatric patients due to the limitations in currently available formulations. Summary The role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute, confirmed measles infection has been well established and is recommended by major medical organizations, including the World Health Organization and American Academy of Pediatrics. Despite the benefits that vitamin A has demonstrated in past studies, treatment with vitamin A remains difficult due to challenges in administration secondary to the limited formulations currently available in the United States. Multiple options exist to extract liquid vitamin A from capsules, but these methods are cumbersome and possess significant challenges. Conclusion Vitamin A treatment should be used in patients with acute, confirmed measles infection, after confirming that they are not at risk for drug interactions and have no symptoms of vitamin A toxicity if they were previously treated with vitamin A. A concentrated liquid formulation of vitamin A approved by the US Food and Drug Administration is needed to overcome current obstacles with administration of vitamin A in pediatric patients unable to swallow capsules.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Purpose Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, the rate of measles infection in 2026 is the highest in more than 3 decades. This clinical consultation explores the role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute measles infection and the challenges posed with this treatment in pediatric patients due to the limitations in currently available formulations. Summary The role of vitamin A in the treatment of acute, confirmed measles infection has been well established and is recommended by major medical organizations, including the World Health Organization and American Academy of Pediatrics. Despite the benefits that vitamin A has demonstrated in past studies, treatment with vitamin A remains difficult due to challenges in administration secondary to the limited formulations currently available in the United States. Multiple options exist to extract liquid vitamin A from capsules, but these methods are cumbersome and possess significant challenges. Conclusion Vitamin A treatment should be used in patients with acute, confirmed measles infection, after confirming that they are not at risk for drug interactions and have no symptoms of vitamin A toxicity if they were previously treated with vitamin A. A concentrated liquid formulation of vitamin A approved by the US Food and Drug Administration is needed to overcome current obstacles with administration of vitamin A in pediatric patients unable to swallow capsules.

papers.title: Evaluation of a dual-intensity measles surveillance system in conflict-affected Borno State, Nigeria.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Maintaining measles surveillance in fragile, conflict-affected settings remains challenging due to insecurity, limited laboratory access and epidemic surges. Borno State, Nigeria, operates a dual-intensity surveillance framework combining laboratory-confirmed case-based surveillance (CBS-Lab) with epidemiologically linked outbreak reporting (CBS-Epi). We evaluated system performance, spatiotemporal surveillance patterns and operational constraints from 2020 to 2024. METHODS: We conducted a programmatic surveillance system evaluation using the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention updated guidelines, assessing system attributes against WHO AFRO benchmarks. The evaluation used retrospective measles surveillance data (28 370 suspected cases) and a cross-sectional survey of surveillance officers assessing perceptual and operational domains (31/58; 53% response), supplemented by a contextual policy document review. Spatiotemporal alignment between surveillance streams was analysed using Spearman's rank correlation. RESULTS: CBS-Lab represented 6.1% (n=1725) of notifications, functioning as a sentinel subset with ≥98% completeness, a 47.8% positive predictive value and 88.4% specimen collection within 48 hours, though only 5% of cases met the <10-day turnaround standard.CBS-Epi (93.9%; n=26 645) maintained ≥99.8% completeness and captured epidemic peaks in 2021 and 2023, though representativeness was constrained by geographic inaccessibility in conflict-affected local government areas. No case-record overlap occurred between streams due to protocol design. Aggregate temporal (ρ=0.69) and geographic (ρ=0.65) co-variations were strong (p<0.001). Laboratory sampling intensity was inversely correlated with district case burden (ρ=-0.64; p<0.001), indicating risk-based prioritisation. Acceptability remained high despite insecurity, transport and funding constraints. CONCLUSION: Within the specific operational context of Borno State, dual-intensity surveillance enabled operationally useful epidemic intelligence and maintained mortality-reduction phase performance despite protracted conflict. These findings suggest that the pragmatic combination of simplified outbreak reporting and targeted laboratory confirmation may represent a feasible surveillance approach in comparable fragile settings, though contextual adaptation would be required.

RESULTS: CBS-Lab represented 6.1% (n=1725) of notifications, functioning as a sentinel subset with ≥98% completeness, a 47.8% positive predictive value and 88.4% specimen collection within 48 hours, though only 5% of cases met the <10-day turnaround standard.CBS-Epi (93.9%; n=26 645) maintained ≥99.8% completeness and captured epidemic peaks in 2021 and 2023, though representativeness was constrained by geographic inaccessibility in conflict-affected local government areas. No case-record overlap occurred between streams due to protocol design. Aggregate temporal (ρ=0.69) and geographic (ρ=0.65) co-variations were strong (p<0.001). Laboratory sampling intensity was inversely correlated with district case burden (ρ=-0.64; p<0.001), indicating risk-based prioritisation. Acceptability remained high despite insecurity, transport and funding constraints. CONCLUSION: Within the specific operational context of Borno State, dual-intensity surveillance enabled operationally useful epidemic intelligence and maintained mortality-reduction phase performance despite protracted conflict. These findings suggest that the pragmatic combination of simplified outbreak reporting and targeted laboratory confirmation may represent a feasible surveillance approach in comparable fragile settings, though contextual adaptation would be required.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:由于不安全、实验室准入有限和流行病激增,在脆弱、受冲突影响的环境中维持 麻疹 监测 仍然具有挑战性。尼日利亚博尔诺州运行双强度 监测 框架,将基于实验室确诊病例的 监测 (CBS-Lab) 与流行病学相关的 暴发 报告 (CBS-Epi) 相结合。我们评估了 2020 年至 2024 年的系统性能、时空 监测 模式和操作限制。方法:我们使用美国疾病控制和预防中心更新的指南进行了程序化 监测 系统评估,根据 WHO AFRO 基准评估系统属性。该评估使用了回顾性 麻疹 监测 数据(28 370 例疑似病例)和对 麻疹 官员评估感知和操作领域的横断面调查(31/58;53% 的回应),并辅以背景政策文件审查。使用 Spearman 等级相关性分析 监测 流之间的时空对齐。结果:CBS-Lab 占通知的 6.1% (n=1725),作为哨兵子集,完整性≥98%,阳性预测值 47.8%,48 小时内收集到 88.4% 的样本,但只有 5% 的病例达到 <10 天的周转标准。CBS-Epi (93.9%;n=26 645) 保持 ≥99.8% 的完整性,尽管代表性受到受冲突影响地方政府地区交通不便的限制,但在 2021 年和 2023 年达到了流行病高峰。由于协议设计,流之间没有发生病例记录重叠。总体时间 (ρ=0.69) 和地理 (ρ=0.65) 协变很强 (p<0.001)。实验室采样强度与地区病例负担呈负相关(ρ=-0.64;p<0.001),表明基于风险的优先顺序。尽管不安全、交通和资金有限,但可接受性仍然很高。结论:在博尔诺州的具体运作背景下,双强度 死亡率 实现了可操作的有用的流行病情报,并在长期冲突的情况下保持了 死亡率 减少阶段的表现。这些发现表明,简化的 暴发 报告和有针对性的实验室确认的务实结合可能代表了在相当脆弱的环境中可行的 监测 方法,尽管需要根据具体情况进行调整。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the clinical management of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) in adults, highlighting the challenges in diagnosing and treating this rare complication of measles virus infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report detailing the management of a single adult patient with SSPE, diagnosed and treated as PRES (Progressive Rubella Encephalopathy Syndrome) due to diagnostic challenges.
analysis.methods: The methods involved clinical evaluation, neurological assessment, and molecular testing to confirm the diagnosis of SSPE, with the patient's clinical data and treatment approach being the primary focus.
analysis.main_results: The patient presented with progressive neurological symptoms and was managed as PRES, but the final diagnosis confirmed it as SSPE caused by measles virus infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the case as highlighting the diagnostic difficulties in distinguishing SSPE from PRES, emphasizing the need for careful clinical and molecular evaluation to ensure accurate management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of accurate diagnosis in managing SSPE, which has significant implications for clinical practice and public health surveillance in measles virus-endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-case design, which may not be generalizable. However, the evidence is strong given the detailed clinical and molecular analysis provided.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes an adult patient with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) who was initially managed as PRES (Progressive Rubella Encephalopathy Syndrome) due to diagnostic challenges. The study highlights the importance of accurate clinical and molecular evaluation in distinguishing SSPE from PRES, which is critical for appropriate management. The findings emphasize the need for vigilance in diagnosing rare complications of measles virus infection, particularly in adults. The study's limitations include its single-case design, which restricts generalizability, but the evidence is considered strong due to the thorough analysis of the patient's clinical data and molecular confirmation of the measles virus as the causative agent. The case contributes to the understanding of SSPE and its differential diagnosis, offering insights for improved clinical practice and public health surveillance.

papers.title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case
papers.abstract: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

papers.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, Practices and Determinants of Measles Vaccination among Mothers of Under-Five Children in Agege Local Government Area, Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Background: Measles remains an important vaccine-preventable cause of childhood morbidity and mortality where vaccination is delayed or incomplete. This study assessed maternal knowledge and attitudes, measles vaccination uptake, and determinants of uptake among mothers of under-five children in Agege Local Government Area (LGA), Lagos State, Nigeria. Methods: A facility-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 308 mothers of under-five children selected through a multistage sampling procedure. Data were collected with a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire and analysed using JASP version 0.98.1. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Cramer's V, odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and multivariable logistic regression were used; statistical significance was set at p < .05. Results: Mean maternal age was 33.7 ± 8.5 years. Good knowledge was recorded in 267 (87%) respondents and 303 (98%) had a positive attitude. Overall measles vaccination uptake was adequate among 282 (92%), although 97 (32%) reported a missed vaccination appointment and 112 (36.4%) reported incomplete scheduled immunization. Knowledge was associated with uptake (χ2 = 15.57, p < .001), whereas attitude was not (χ2 = 0.469, p = .494). In the adjusted model, occupation, number of under-five children, knowledge status, waiting time, work schedule, information gaps, cultural beliefs, family-elder influence, religious beliefs and community norms were statistically significant (p < .05); several estimates had very wide CIs and therefore require cautious interpretation. Conclusion: Maternal knowledge, attitudes and reported measles vaccination uptake were high, but missed appointments, incomplete immunization and practical, informational and sociocultural barriers persisted. Programmes should combine accurate health education with shorter waiting times, flexible service delivery, defaulter tracking and family/community engagement.
papers.journal: International Journal of Global Health and Epidemiology

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:麻疹 仍然是儿童发病的重要 疫苗 可预防原因,而 死亡率 则 疫苗接种 延迟或不完整。本研究评估了尼日利亚拉各斯州阿杰地方政府区 (LGA) 5 岁以下儿童母亲的母亲知识和态度、麻疹 麻疹 的吸收情况以及吸收的决定因素。方法:对通过多阶段抽样程序选出的 308 名 5 岁以下儿童的母亲进行了一项基于机构的描述性横断面研究。通过结构化访谈问卷收集数据,并使用 JASP 0.98.1 版本进行分析。使用描述性统计、卡方检验、Cramer V、95% 置信区间 (CI) 的比值比以及多变量逻辑回归;统计显着性设置为 p < .05。结果:产妇平均年龄为 33.7 ± 8.5 岁。267 名(87%)受访者记录了良好的知识,303 名(98%)受访者持积极态度。尽管 97 人 (32%) 报告错过了 麻疹 疫苗接种 预约,112 人 (36.4%) 报告计划免疫接种不完整,但 282 人 (92%) 的总体 麻疹 疫苗接种 吸收率充足。知识与吸收相关(χ2 = 15.57,p < .001),而态度则不然(χ2 = 0.469,p = .494)。在调整后的模型中,职业、五岁以下儿童数量、知识状况、等待时间、工作时间表、信息差距、文化信仰、家庭长辈影响、宗教信仰和社区规范具有统计显着性(p < .05);一些估计值的置信区间非常宽,因此需要谨慎解释。结论:母亲的知识、态度和报告的 麻疹 疫苗接种 吸收率很高,但错过预约、免疫不完全以及实际、信息和社会文化障碍仍然存在。计划应将准确的健康教育与更短的等待时间、灵活的服务提供、违约者跟踪和家庭/社区参与结合起来。

papers.title: Beyond the first dose: socioeconomic inequality in pentavalent and measles vaccine dropout among Nigerian children, evidence from the 2023–24 Demographic and Health Survey
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Few countries have as many under-immunised children as Nigeria. Catch-up programmes rightly prioritise zero-dose children, but children who begin the schedule and then fall away form a large, readily traceable group whose distribution is poorly understood. We estimated dropout from the first to the third dose of pentavalent vaccine (Penta1–Penta3) and from the first to the second dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1–MCV2), measured wealth-related inequality in each, and identified the factors that account for it. Methods From the children's file of the 2023–24 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, we drew two samples: 3,164 Penta1 recipients aged 12–23 months and 2,314 MCV1 recipients aged 24–35 months. We estimated design-adjusted prevalences, measured inequality with the Erreygers corrected concentration index, identified correlates with survey-weighted logistic regression, and apportioned inequality among them by regression-based decomposition. Results Coverage reached 53.8% for Penta3 and 30.5% for MCV2. Of children who started each series, 14.5% did not complete pentavalent vaccination and 36.6% did not receive MCV2. Penta dropout was 17% in the poorest and 8% in the richest quintile; for measles the figures were 46% and 31%. Dropout was concentrated among poorer children (Erreygers index − 0.083 for Penta and − 0.105 for MCV), but much less strongly than first-dose coverage was concentrated among richer children (Penta1 + 0.422). Penta dropout odds were lower in the richest households (aOR 0.37, 95% CI 0.21–0.66) and with higher maternal education (aOR 0.40, 0.23–0.71), and higher for urban children once wealth was considered (aOR 2.35, 1.70–3.26). Wealth and maternal education contributed most to inequality in both outcomes, and place of delivery contributed substantially for MCV. Conclusions Most of the wealth-related inequity in Nigeria's immunisation programme arises when children enter the schedule, but it does not disappear after first contact and is greater in the second year of life. Services should trace defaulters, strengthen the second-year-of-life contact and target the urban poor, children of less-educated mothers and children born at home.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that wealth and maternal education were the most significant contributors to inequality in both outcomes, and place of delivery contributed substantially for MCV. The findings suggest that services should trace defaulters, strengthen the second-year-of-life contact, and target the urban poor, children of less-educated mothers, and those born at home.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解尼日利亚儿童中 疫苗 辍学儿童的社会经济不平等,重点关注五价和 麻疹 疫苗。很少有国家像尼日利亚一样拥有如此多的免疫不足儿童,而补习计划往往会忽视那些未能遵守 疫苗接种 计划的儿童。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了 2023-24 年尼日利亚人口和健康调查的数据,抽取了两个样本:3,164 名 12-23 个月大的 Penta1 接受者和 2,314 名 24-35 个月大的 MCV1 接受者。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员估计了设计调整后的 患病率,用 Erreygers 校正集中指数测量了不平等,确定了与调查加权逻辑回归的相关性,并通过基于回归的分解在它们之间分配了不平等。
elements_zh.main_results: Penta3 的覆盖率达到 53.8%,MCV2 的覆盖率达到 30.5%。在开始每个系列的儿童中,14.5% 没有完成五价 疫苗接种,36.6% 没有接受 MCV2。最贫困人口的 Penta 辍学率为 17%,最富有的五分之一人口的辍学率为 8%;麻疹 的数字分别为 46% 和 31%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,财富和母亲教育是造成这两种结果不平等的最重要因素,而分娩地点对 MCV 的影响很大。研究结果表明,服务应追踪违约者,加强与二年级孩子的联系,并针对城市贫民、母亲受教育程度较低的孩子以及在家出生的孩子。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为 监测、诊断 和 治疗 策略提供信息,以提高 疫苗接种 覆盖率并减少免疫规划中的社会经济不平等。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计局限性包括使用自我报告的数据和潜在的回忆偏差。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Measles resurgence in England: challenges in maintaining elimination, 2023 to 2024
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Between October 2023 and September 2024, England experienced the largest measles outbreak in decades. AIM We describe the epidemiology of the outbreak, burden on secondary care services and the factors that led to this resurgence. METHODS The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) conducts enhanced surveillance of all suspected measles cases in England. A measles line list was established using routinely collected notification, laboratory, demographic and vaccination information. Laboratory-confirmed cases were defined using serology and PCR. Incidence rates were calculated using mid-2024 population estimates. Severity was assessed through linkage with emergency department attendances, hospital admissions and length of stay. RESULTS Most of the 2,821 laboratory-confirmed cases resided in London (n = 1,283; 45.5%) and in the West Midlands (n = 710; 25.2%). Incidence was highest in London (14.1/100,000 population). Children under 10 years represented 58.6% (n = 1,653) of cases. Most cases (n = 2,609; 92.5%) were not vaccinated, and 63.0% (n = 1,776) lived in areas belonging to the two most deprived quintiles. Of the 2,788 cases that could be linked to hospitalisation data, 76.3% (n = 2,127) attended emergency care and 38.2% (n = 1,066) were admitted. Median length of stay was 2.0 days, seven cases received intensive care; one death was reported. Admissions were highest among infants aged CONCLUSION This outbreak reflects a shift towards endemic measles transmission in areas of high deprivation and low vaccine uptake in England. It underscores the importance of achieving 95% uptake with measles vaccine in all areas and communities to achieve and maintain elimination.

Children under 10 years accounted for 58.6% of cases, and the majority were unvaccinated. Hospitalisation data showed that 76.3% of cases required emergency care, with 38.2% admitted. papers.full_text: Article summary The resurgence of measles in Bangladesh in 2026 highlights the fragility of immunization systems, revealing how quickly gains in disease elimination can be reversed due to declining vaccination coverage and systemic failures. This paper outlines the outbreak's drivers and consequences, emphasizing the urgent need for policy reforms focused on equitable vaccine access, improved governance, and robust immunization strategies to prevent future crises. Abstract Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in decades, with more than 50,500 suspected cases and at least 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths during the reporting period from mid-March to mid-May 2026. After years of progress that had sharply reduced measles incidence, this resurgence reflects not a biological inevitability but a preventable systems failure. A nationwide Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine stockout in 2024 to 2025, the absence of nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) since 2020, declining MR1 and MR2 coverage, and widening subnational inequities have combined to erode population immunity. The burden has fallen disproportionately on zero-dose and under-vaccinated children in urban slums, hard-to-reach rural areas, and refugee camps, especially infants too young for routine vaccination. Positioned within the broader post-COVID global resurgence, Bangladesh’s epidemic highlights measles as a sentinel of weakening immunization resilience. The crisis underscores three transferable lessons for countries facing declining coverage: maintain buffer stocks and diversified procurement to prevent stockouts, prioritize catch-up SIAs when routine coverage falters, and embed equity-focused outreach to reach zero-dose children before outbreaks occur. This perspective article delves into the structural reforms needed in vaccine governance and procurement, the restoration of routine and catch-up immunization services with equity at their center, and the transparent accountability required to address the failures that created the current immunity gap. Similar content being viewed by others 1 Introduction Globally, measles remains a major threat despite an available vaccine, with an estimated 11 million cases and 95,000 deaths in 2024 and outbreaks reported in 59 countries, underscoring WHO’s recommendation that ≥ 95% coverage with two measles-containing vaccine doses is required to interrupt transmission [1]. Bangladesh was long seen as a regional model for measles control, with substantial gains driven by sustained routine immunization and periodic supplementary campaigns. Yet the country is now confronting one of its most severe measles outbreaks in decades, exposing how quickly immunization gains can unravel when coverage declines, vaccine supply is disrupted, and inequities persist [2, 3]. This resurgence has had devastating consequences for children, particularly in underserved and hard-to-reach communities where routine services are weakest and vulnerability is highest [4]. This perspective examines the drivers of Bangladesh’s 2026 measles resurgence, situates it within the wider post-COVID global rebound in measles, and argues that durable control will require equity-centered reform of immunization governance, delivery, and accountability. It further contends that the outbreak should be read not as an isolated epidemiologic event, but as a warning signal of broader fragility in child health systems and public health preparedness [5]. 2 Reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains 2.1 Earlier progress towards elimination In the early 2000s, measles remained a leading cause of child mortality in Bangladesh, with national first dose of measles‐containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage stagnating at or below 75% and no district achieving the 95% threshold required for population-level protection. Through sustained investment in EPI, linkage with child health days and vitamin A campaigns, and repeated nationwide SIAs, Bangladesh raised MCV1 coverage from roughly 74–89% in 2000 to more than 94–118% (administrative) by 2016. At the same time, a routine second dose (MCV2) was introduced in 2012 and the coverage of MCV2 increased from roughly one-third of children to over 90% by the mid-2010s. Over the same period, confirmed measles incidence declined by more than 80%, decreasing from approximately 40 cases per million population to 6 per million, and large outbreaks became rare [6, 7]. At the regional level, the WHO South-East Asia Region established targets for measles elimination and rubella control. Bangladesh aligned with these goals, committing to elimination timelines initially set for 2018 and subsequently extended, thereby firmly integrating measles control into national child survival strategies and Universal Health Coverage priorities. These achievements positioned Bangladesh as a model of immunization success in a low-income setting and fostered momentum toward increasingly ambitious elimination targets [6, 8]. 2.2 Slow erosion of population immunity Behind this success story, however, vulnerabilities began to accumulate. WHO and national surveillance data indicate that although national MR1 and MR2 coverage remained relatively high, both measures plateaued and then fell modestly after 2019, MR1 from about 88–89% to 86%, and MR2 from roughly 89% to 80.7% by 2023–2024, leaving an estimated 20 million children partially or fully unprotected during this period [9]. These national averages masked substantial subnational inequities. Urban slums, hard-to-reach rural unions, and humanitarian settings, including the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, continued to harbor concentrations of zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, underscoring persistent access and equity gaps despite overall coverage gains. Moreover, although Bangladesh historically conducted SIAs at roughly four-year intervals, no nationwide MR campaign was carried out after 2020, largely because of pandemic-related disruptions and subsequent political instability [10, 11]. 3 The 2024 to 2025 MR vaccine stockout, a preventable disruption 3.1 Procurement disruption and stockout Multiple reports from WHO, UNICEF, and subsequent investigations suggest that disruptions in MR vaccine supply and immunization delivery during 2024–2025 may have contributed to the accumulation of susceptible children before the 2026 outbreak. Following the 2024 political transition, changes in procurement arrangements and reported administrative delays were associated with vaccine stockouts and interruptions in routine immunization [2, 12]. A supplementary MR campaign postponed in 2024 was reportedly not implemented in 2025 and was subsequently cancelled. Available coverage estimates are inconsistent: WHO–UNICEF reported MR1 and MR2 coverage of 97% and 93% in 2023, whereas some national reports cited a decline to approximately 56–59% in 2025 [13, 14]. These discrepancies may reflect differences in data sources and methods. Overall, the evidence suggests, but does not establish that these disruptions likely expanded the susceptible population and facilitated the outbreak’s scale. 3.2 Missed SIAs and compounded immunity gaps The stockout occurred against the backdrop of missed SIAs after 2020, when COVID-19 and subsequent political unrest delayed the usual four-yearly nationwide campaigns. Without these catch-up campaigns to reach zero-dose and missed children, each year of modest under‐coverage added to a growing cohort of susceptible children. By early 2026, WHO estimated that suboptimal MR1 and MR2 coverage, combined with the absence of SIAs and the 2024–2025 vaccine stockout, had significantly increased the number of susceptible children. This convergence of vulnerabilities created favorable conditions for sustained measles transmission once the virus reentered the population. The measles virus, being one of the most contagious pathogens known, readily exploits such immunity gaps, and outbreaks are often the earliest visible indication of deeper fragility in the immunization system [15, 16]. 4 Epidemiologic scale and clinical burden of the 2026 measles outbreak 4.1 Epidemiology and severity On 4 April 2026, Bangladesh’s National International Health Regulations (IHR) Focal Point notified WHO of a nationwide increase in measles cases. By 11 May 2026, DGHS data reported 50,500 suspected cases and 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths, giving a crude reported death-to-suspected-case ratio of approximately 0.82% [2]. The majority of cases, approximately 79%, occurred in children under five years of age, including 66% in those under two years and about one-third in infants younger than nine months, an age group that is not yet eligible for routine measles vaccination. Subsequent situation reports from national authorities, the World Health Organization, and humanitarian partners indicate sustained expansion of the outbreak. Between 22 April and 4 May 2026, reported cumulative suspected measles cases in Bangladesh rose from 27,164 to 41,793, while laboratory-confirmed cases increased from 3,934 to 5,467. Over the same period, the reported combined toll of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths rose from 190 to 311. Children under five accounted for approximately 80% of reported cases as of 19 April [17]. Daily hospital admissions have, at times, exceeded 1,200–1,300 cases, overwhelming pediatric services and exposing critical shortages in isolation capacity, healthcare personnel, and diagnostic resources [2, 18]. Measles-associated complications, including pneumonia, diarrhoea, and severe disease linked to malnutrition, are frequently reported, particularly among undernourished children and those lacking vitamin A supplementation. This pattern is consistent with global evidence demonstrating that measles-related mortality disproportionately affects vulnerable, malnourished populations. Although precise case fatality ratios vary by setting and surveillance sensitivity, the concentration of deaths among unvaccinated and under-vaccinated children under two years of age underscores the largely preventable nature of this burden [19]. 4.2 Spatial concentration and social determinants The outbreak has attained extensive geographic spread, affecting 58 of 64 districts, approximately 91%, across all eight divisions, while remaining highly concentrated in specific hotspots (Fig. 1). Dhaka division alone has reported over 18,000 to 19,000 cases in several situation reports, with substantial burdens also observed in Rajshahi, Chattogram, and Khulna. Within Dhaka, cases are concentrated in densely populated informal settlements and industrial slums, including Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon, where crowding, poverty, and highly mobile populations complicate the delivery of routine health services [2, 20]. Humanitarian settings, particularly the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, constitute a major concern during the 2026 measles outbreak in Bangladesh. In the camps, measles transmission was documented early in the outbreak and then escalated rapidly, with reports noting 19 suspected cases in January, 199 in February, 76 suspected cases with 8 laboratory-confirmed cases by March, and 239 suspected cases tested with 60 confirmed cases and 5 associated deaths by 14 May 2026. By 20 May 2026, the camp setting had reported 595 suspected and 60 confirmed cases, underscoring the intense transmission potential in a population with constrained access to routine services, heavy reliance on humanitarian assistance, high baseline malnutrition, large zero-dose cohorts, and frequent population movement. These conditions create a setting highly conducive to explosive measles spread and severe clinical outcomes [2, 21]. 5 Determinants of the catastrophe 5.1 Programmatic and health‐system determinants From a programmatic perspective, three interlocking determinants stand out. Suboptimal routine immunization coverage and missed SIAs have created a major vulnerability, as measles elimination requires at least 95% two-dose coverage in every district. Available estimates suggest that MR1 and MR2 coverage in Bangladesh may have declined to approximately 57–59% in 2025, potentially leaving a substantial susceptible population and facilitating sustained transmission. Reported nationwide MR vaccine stockouts during 2024–2025, reportedly associated with changes in procurement arrangements and administrative delays, may represent an important health-system weakness that contributed to reduced immunization opportunities and may have affected public confidence in services. In addition, possible gaps in surveillance and delays in recognizing early increases in measles incidence during late 2025 and early 2026 may have limited the timeliness of national alerting and pre-emptive campaigns, although the precise contribution of these factors is difficult to establish from the available evidence. These programmatic challenges may reflect broader health-system constraints, including potentially inadequate buffer stocks and contingency planning, limited operational flexibility of the EPI, and persistent underinvestment in peripheral human resources and cold-chain capacity; further evaluation is needed to confirm their relative contributions to the outbreak [22]. 5.2 Social and structural determinants Social determinants strongly shaped both measles exposure and outcomes in Bangladesh during the 2026 outbreak. Children living in urban slums, peri-urban settlements, and remote rural areas faced multiple barriers to vaccination, including distance to facilities, opportunity costs for caregivers in informal work, gendered constraints on women’s mobility, and low trust in preventive services amid precarious livelihoods. These structural barriers were not evenly distributed: WHO reported that the outbreak’s cumulative burden in Dhaka was concentrated in dense informal settlements, including Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon, underscoring how overcrowding and deprivation amplified transmission risk. Similarly, a WHO-supported campaign in Gopalganj identified at least 16 eligible children from mobile “floating” families who had missed both routine immunization and the outbreak campaign entirely, illustrating how mobile and marginalized households can remain outside the reach of standard delivery systems. These same children are also more likely to be undernourished, vitamin A deficient, and living in overcrowded housing, increasing both infection risk and disease severity once infected. The crisis further exposed inequities in humanitarian protection: Rohingya children in the camps, undocumented migrants, and mobile populations along the India and Myanmar borders were repeatedly at risk of being missed by routine services and campaigns, while large zero-dose cohorts and cross-border mobility continued to sustain transmission [2, 23]. 6 Post-COVID global measles resurgence Bangladesh’s outbreak is part of a broader global resurgence rather than an isolated event. Regional comparisons underscore that Bangladesh’s 2026 outbreak was part of a wider measles resurgence in South-East Asia, with WHO documenting outbreaks or increases in measles cases in India, Nepal, Thailand, and Maldives, and Myanmar strengthening measles preparedness in border areas because of spillover risk from Bangladesh. In the post-COVID period, measles has re-expanded sharply worldwide, and WHO reported that 59 countries experienced large or disruptive outbreaks in 2024, nearly three times the number in 2021, including several that had previously achieved elimination. Global MCV1 coverage in 2024, at approximately 84 to 86%, and MCV2 coverage, at about 76%, remained below pre pandemic levels and far short of the 95% two dose threshold needed to interrupt transmission. The Bangladesh epidemic thus exemplifies a broader pattern: measles serves as a sensitive indicator of weaknesses in immunization systems, because its extreme contagiousness means that even small gaps in routine coverage or outbreak response can rapidly lead to sustained transmission. Even modest and sustained declines in coverage, especially when compounded by missed campaigns, can quickly accumulate large susceptible cohorts and precipitate explosive outbreaks once importation or reemergence occurs [2, 24, 25]. 7 Policy and governance implications 7.1 Accountability for procurement and stock management Reports of vaccine procurement delays and stockouts, alongside indications of reduced measles vaccination coverage in 2025, raise questions about the continuity and governance of Bangladesh’s immunization programme [25]. Reporting in May 2026 suggested that proposed changes to established procurement arrangements may have contributed to supply delays, although the nature and effects of those changes remained contested. Leaders of the newly elected government also discussed responsibility across previous administrations and interim authorities in parliamentary remarks. Taken together, these accounts point to a need to examine procurement decisions and their possible contribution to coverage gaps, rather than to presume a single cause. They also highlight the value of clearly assigned procurement authority, transparent stock monitoring, adequate buffer inventories, and continuity plans to protect EPI vaccine supply during policy or institutional transitions [26]. 7.2 Communication, trust, and community engagement Unlike in some high-income countries, available evidence suggests that widespread anti-vaccine sentiment is not the principal driver of measles resurgence in Bangladesh. Instead, most available reports emphasize structural access and supply barriers more than active refusal. Nevertheless, effective communication and community engagement remain essential to sustain trust, improve uptake, and support outbreak control. Reports or concerns about vaccine…

papers.title_original: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh 2026 undermines elimination gains and requires urgent policy action

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh, which undermines previous elimination gains and necessitates urgent policy action. The background highlights the ongoing threat of measles globally, despite the availability of a vaccine, and the importance of achieving high vaccination coverage to interrupt transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examines the reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains, focusing on the period from the early 2000s to 2026. It includes a population of children in Bangladesh, with data collected through sustained investment in the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), linkage with child health days, and repeated nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs).
analysis.methods: The methods involve the analysis of national and WHO surveillance data, including coverage estimates of measles-containing vaccines (MCV1 and MCV2), and the examination of reported cases and deaths. The study also considers the impact of changes in procurement arrangements and administrative delays on vaccine stockouts and routine immunization.
analysis.main_results: The main results show a significant increase in measles cases and deaths in early 2026, with 50,500 suspected cases and 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths. The majority of cases occurred in children under five years of age, with a high concentration in Dhaka division. The study also reports a decline in routine immunization coverage and the absence of SIAs, which contributed to the resurgence of measles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating a major vulnerability in Bangladesh’s measles elimination efforts, with suboptimal coverage and missed SIAs creating a susceptible population. The study highlights the need for urgent policy action to address these issues and prevent further outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh has significant implications for public health, including the potential for further spread and the need for enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts. The study underscores the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage to prevent measles outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations, including inconsistent coverage estimates and the potential for delays in recognizing early increases in measles incidence. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on reported data and the absence of specific methodological details.

analysis.summary_en: The study examines the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh, which undermines previous elimination gains and necessitates urgent policy action. Key findings include a significant increase in cases and deaths, with suboptimal vaccination coverage and missed SIAs contributing to the resurgence. The study highlights the need for enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts to prevent further outbreaks.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh, which undermines previous elimination gains and necessitates urgent policy action. The background highlights the ongoing threat of measles globally, despite the availability of a vaccine, and the importance of achieving high vaccination coverage to interrupt transmission.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study examines the reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains, focusing on the period from the early 2000s to 2026. It includes a population of children in Bangladesh, with data collected through sustained investment in the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), linkage with child health days, and repeated nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs).
analysis_en.methods: The methods involve the analysis of national and WHO surveillance data, including coverage estimates of measles-containing vaccines (MCV1 and MCV2), and the examination of reported cases and deaths. The study also considers the impact of changes in procurement arrangements and administrative delays on vaccine stockouts and routine immunization.
analysis_en.main_results: The main results show a significant increase in measles cases and deaths in early 2026, with 50,500 suspected cases and 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths. The majority of cases occurred in children under five years of age, with a high concentration in Dhaka division. The study also reports a decline in routine immunization coverage and the absence of SIAs, which contributed to the resurgence of measles.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating a major vulnerability in Bangladesh’s measles elimination efforts, with suboptimal coverage and missed SIAs creating a susceptible population. The study highlights the need for urgent policy action to address these issues and prevent further outbreaks.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh has significant implications for public health, including the potential for further spread and the need for enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts. The study underscores the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage to prevent measles outbreaks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations, including inconsistent coverage estimates and the potential for delays in recognizing early increases in measles incidence. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on reported data and the absence of specific methodological details.

Article summary The resurgence of measles in Bangladesh in 2026 highlights the fragility of immunization systems, revealing how quickly gains in disease elimination can be reversed due to declining vaccination coverage and systemic failures. This paper outlines the outbreak's drivers and consequences, emphasizing the urgent need for policy reforms focused on equitable vaccine access, improved governance, and robust immunization strategies to prevent future crises. Abstract Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in decades, with more than 50,500 suspected cases and at least 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths during the reporting period from mid-March to mid-May 2026. After years of progress that had sharply reduced measles incidence, this resurgence reflects not a biological inevitability but a preventable systems failure. A nationwide Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine stockout in 2024 to 2025, the absence of nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) since 2020, declining MR1 and MR2 coverage, and widening subnational inequities have combined to erode population immunity. The burden has fallen disproportionately on zero-dose and under-vaccinated children in urban slums, hard-to-reach rural areas, and refugee camps, especially infants too young for routine vaccination. Positioned within the broader post-COVID global resurgence, Bangladesh’s epidemic highlights measles as a sentinel of weakening immunization resilience. papers.title: Measles resurgence in Italy: analysis of temporal patterns of viral transmission, surveillance performance, and vaccination coverage at national and regional levels, October 2023 to March 2025
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Following substantial progress towards measles elimination after the COVID-19 pandemic, Italy experienced a marked increase in measles cases in 2024. AIM Our aim was to describe measles epidemiology in Italy, October 2023–March 2025, and assess vaccination coverage, surveillance performance at national and regional levels, and temporal patterns of transmission. METHODS Numbers of measles cases and outbreaks were reviewed. Vaccination coverage and surveillance indicators were described at national and regional levels. Measles variants were classified by genotype and Distinct Sequence Identifier (DSId). Temporal transmission patterns of measles variants were assessed nationally and regionally to identify sustained transmission chains (≥ 12 consecutive months). RESULTS In total, 1,311 measles cases were reported, with 178 outbreaks. Cases’ median age was 30.9 years (IQR: 15.6–39.8); 601 were female (45.8%) and 710 male (54.2%). Only 3.1% (38/1,230) were fully vaccinated. In 2024, the first-dose vaccination coverage increased to 94.77% (95% CI: 94.70–94.84%) nationally, while second-dose coverage declined to 84.45% (95% CI: 84.35–84.55%). Among all cases, 12.1% (n = 158) were imported/importation-related, 64.1% (n = 841) were of unknown origin and 52.8% had DSId data available (n = 692), with high regional heterogeneity. Twenty-five measles variants were identified. One variant (D8–5963) showed sustained national transmission for over 12 months, meeting criteria for re-established endemic transmission, although no single region showed uninterrupted ≥ 12-month circulation. CONCLUSION Measles resurgence in Italy was marked by persistent immunity gaps, heterogeneous surveillance performance, and sustained national circulation of a D8 variant, indicating loss of near-elimination status. Strengthening vaccination strategies and enhancing molecular surveillance is urgently needed to restore progress towards measles elimination.

papers.title_zh: 麻疹 在意大利卷土重来:2023 年 10 月至 2025 年 3 月期间病毒 传播、监测 表现以及 疫苗接种 在国家和地区层面覆盖的时间模式分析
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Following substantial progress towards measles elimination after the COVID-19 pandemic, Italy experienced a marked increase in measles cases in 2024. AIM Our aim was to describe measles epidemiology in Italy, October 2023–March 2025, and assess vaccination coverage, surveillance performance at national and regional levels, and temporal patterns of transmission. METHODS Numbers of measles cases and outbreaks were reviewed. Vaccination coverage and surveillance indicators were described at national and regional levels. Measles variants were classified by genotype and Distinct Sequence Identifier (DSId). Temporal transmission patterns of measles variants were assessed nationally and regionally to identify sustained transmission chains (≥ 12 consecutive months). RESULTS In total, 1,311 measles cases were reported, with 178 outbreaks. Cases’ median age was 30.9 years (IQR: 15.6–39.8); 601 were female (45.8%) and 710 male (54.2%). Only 3.1% (38/1,230) were fully vaccinated. In 2024, the first-dose vaccination coverage increased to 94.77% (95% CI: 94.70–94.84%) nationally, while second-dose coverage declined to 84.45% (95% CI: 84.35–84.55%). Among all cases, 12.1% (n = 158) were imported/importation-related, 64.1% (n = 841) were of unknown origin and 52.8% had DSId data available (n = 692), with high regional heterogeneity. Twenty-five measles variants were identified. One variant (D8–5963) showed sustained national transmission for over 12 months, meeting criteria for re-established endemic transmission, although no single region showed uninterrupted ≥ 12-month circulation. CONCLUSION Measles resurgence in Italy was marked by persistent immunity gaps, heterogeneous surveillance performance, and sustained national circulation of a D8 variant, indicating loss of near-elimination status. Strengthening vaccination strategies and enhancing molecular surveillance is urgently needed to restore progress towards measles elimination.

papers.title: MEASLES-INDUCED SUBACUTE SCLEROSING PANENCEPHALITIS (DAWSON'S DISEASE): CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND DIAGNOSTICS
papers.abstract: Introduction: Measles is characterized by high contagiousness. One of its rarest but most lethal complications is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), which primarily occurs in children and adolescents. The frequency among infected individuals is 1:10,000, while in vaccinated individuals, it is exceptionally rare (~1:500,000). Pathogenesis and Course: The main feature of the disease is an atypically long, 6–15-year asymptomatic period between the contracted measles infection and the onset of panencephalitis. The persistence of the virus in neural tissues and the disruption of the immune response lead to progressively worsening psychoneurological damage. The clinical course includes 4 stages: behavioral changes and headaches, seizures, severe movement coordination disorders (ataxia, myoclonus), and coma caused by brainstem damage, leading to a fatal outcome (on average within 3 years). Diagnostics: The diagnosis is based on the medical history, characteristic Radermecker complexes on the electroencephalogram (EEG), a sharply elevated titer of measles-specific IgG antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid and blood, and demyelination revealed by MRI. Conclusion: Panencephalitis represents the most severe complication of measles. Despite modern diagnostic methods, the disease is progressive and fatal, with universal vaccination remaining its only effective prevention measure.

papers.title_zh: 麻疹 诱发的 亚急性硬化性全脑炎(道森病):临床特征和诊断
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Measles is characterized by high contagiousness. One of its rarest but most lethal complications is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), which primarily occurs in children and adolescents. The frequency among infected individuals is 1:10,000, while in vaccinated individuals, it is exceptionally rare (~1:500,000). Pathogenesis and Course: The main feature of the disease is an atypically long, 6–15-year asymptomatic period between the contracted measles infection and the onset of panencephalitis. The persistence of the virus in neural tissues and the disruption of the immune response lead to progressively worsening psychoneurological damage. The clinical course includes 4 stages: behavioral changes and headaches, seizures, severe movement coordination disorders (ataxia, myoclonus), and coma caused by brainstem damage, leading to a fatal outcome (on average within 3 years). Diagnostics: The diagnosis is based on the medical history, characteristic Radermecker complexes on the electroencephalogram (EEG), a sharply elevated titer of measles-specific IgG antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid and blood, and demyelination revealed by MRI. Conclusion: Panencephalitis represents the most severe complication of measles. Despite modern diagnostic methods, the disease is progressive and fatal, with universal vaccination remaining its only effective prevention measure.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:麻疹的特点是传染性高。亚急性硬化性全脑炎 (SSPE) 是其最罕见但最致命的并发症之一,主要发生在儿童和青少年中。感染者中的发生频率为 1:10,000,而在接种疫苗的个体中,这种情况极为罕见(~1:500,000)。麻疹 和病程:该疾病的主要特征是从感染 麻疹 到全脑炎发作之间有一段异常漫长的 6-15 年无症状期。病毒在神经组织中的持续存在和 免疫应答 的破坏导致精神神经损伤逐渐恶化。临床过程包括4个阶段:行为改变和头痛、癫痫发作、严重运动协调障碍(共济失调、肌阵挛)以及脑干损伤引起的昏迷,导致致命结果(平均3年内)。诊断:麻疹 基于病史、脑电图 (EEG) 上的特征性 Radermecker 复合物、脑脊液和血液中 麻疹 特异性 IgG 抗体滴度急剧升高以及 MRI 显示的脱髓鞘情况。结论:全脑炎是麻疹最严重的并发症。尽管有现代诊断方法,但这种疾病是进行性和致命性的,通用 疫苗接种 仍然是唯一有效的预防措施。

papers.title: Measles Vaccination Coverage and Vaccine Exemptions Before Ontario’s 2024–2025 Outbreak: An Analysis of Case Rates Across Public Health Units
papers.abstract: Time-stamped analysis plan for an exploratory ecological study of measles vaccination coverage, vaccine exemptions and outbreak case rates across Ontario’s 29 public health units during the 2024–2025 measles outbreak. The study uses publicly available aggregate data from Public Health Ontario (outbreak cases by public health unit; school-based measles coverage and exemption estimates for 7- and 17-year-olds) and Statistics Canada (population estimates). The plan was lodged before any statistical modelling. Public health unit exposure values and outbreak case rates had already been inspected, which prompted the documented amendment in version 2 (removal of the primary/secondary exposure hierarchy and addition of data-quality caveats). This is therefore not a fully prospective preregistration, and all association analyses are exploratory.
