papers.full_text: Dear Editor, Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent infection of the central nervous system by a mutated measles virus.[] The disease classically presents with cognitive decline, behavioral deterioration, progressive impairment of scholastic performance, and stereotyped periodic myoclonus.[,] However, accumulating evidence indicates that the clinical spectrum of SSPE is considerably broader than previously recognized, and movement disorders may occasionally dominate the clinical presentation, leading to substantial diagnostic challenges.[] Hyperkinetic and hypokinetic movement disorders, including chorea, athetosis, dystonia, tremor, parkinsonism, and various mixed phenomenologies, have all been described in association with SSPE.[] In some patients, these manifestations may overshadow the characteristic myoclonic jerks and mimic primary movement disorders, autoimmune encephalitis, or neurodegenerative diseases, resulting in delayed diagnosis.[,] A 9-year-old boy was referred to the pediatric neurology clinic because of progressively worsening gait instability and involuntary movements that had developed over several months. According to his parents, he initially exhibited unsteadiness while walking, difficulty in changing direction, and intermittent truncal swaying. Over the following weeks, the involuntary movements became increasingly prominent, interfering with daily activities and leading to a marked decline in school performance. Clinical evaluation revealed progressive cognitive deterioration and behavioral changes accompanied by frequent involuntary movements. The patient experienced recurrent, sudden, brief, stereotyped myoclonic jerks predominantly involving the upper extremities and trunk. These episodes occurred multiple times throughout the day and occasionally disrupted gait and routine activities. His medical history was unremarkable, with no prior neurological illness. Vaccinations had been administered according to the National Immunization Schedule. Neurological examination demonstrated marked axial instability. The patient had difficulty in maintaining postural control while standing and exhibited a broad-based, unsteady gait. Frequent brief myoclonic jerks involving the trunk and upper limbs were observed [Video 1]. In addition, intermittent dystonic posturing of the upper extremities was noted. Irregular, flowing, and twisting choreoathetoid movements became particularly evident during voluntary actions. These movements varied in amplitude and occasionally spread from distal to proximal muscle groups. Given the predominance of hyperkinetic movement abnormalities, the initial diagnostic considerations included a primary movement disorder, neurodegenerative disease, or autoimmune encephalitis. Nevertheless, the progressive clinical course and accompanying cognitive decline suggested an underlying diffuse central nervous system disorder. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was entirely normal, with no detectable cortical, subcortical, white matter, or basal ganglia abnormalities. In contrast, electroencephalography revealed stereotyped, bilaterally synchronous, high-amplitude generalized periodic complexes recurring at regular intervals over a diffusely slowed background rhythm [Figure 1]. These characteristic periodic discharges represented the classic electroencephalographic hallmark of SSPE and strongly supported the diagnosis. Subsequent evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated anti-measles antibody titers in both cerebrospinal fluid and serum, confirming the diagnosis. Although periodic myoclonus remains the most recognized manifestation of SSPE, movement disorders may emerge at various stages of the disease and occasionally become the predominant clinical feature.[] In a large clinical series, Prashanth et al.[] documented a wide spectrum of movement disorders in patients with SSPE, including dystonia, chorea, tremor, and parkinsonism. Importantly, the authors emphasized that these manifestations were not limited to advanced disease stages and could dominate the initial clinical presentation.[] Similarly, Jagtap et al.[] reported that dystonic and choreiform movements may occasionally be more prominent than myoclonus, thereby obscuring the diagnosis. More recently, a systematic review by Garg et al.[] highlighted the remarkable heterogeneity of movement disorder phenomenology in SSPE and underscored the importance of recognizing atypical presentations. The pathophysiological basis of movement disorders in SSPE remains incompletely understood. However, involvement of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and cortico-striatal networks is believed to play a central role.[] Neuropathological studies have demonstrated degeneration and inflammatory changes within basal ganglia circuits, which may contribute to the development of hyperkinetic movement disorders.[] Neuroimaging studies have further suggested that thalamic and basal ganglia dysfunction may underlie the emergence of dystonia, chorea, and other abnormal movements.[,] Nevertheless, structural neuroimaging findings may be entirely normal, particularly during the early stages of the disease.[] The absence of MRI abnormalities in our patient likely reflects microscopic pathological changes that remain below the detection threshold of conventional imaging techniques.[] A particularly noteworthy aspect of the present case was the striking predominance of movement disorder manifestations. Video analysis demonstrated severe axial instability, dystonic posturing, choreoathetoid movements, and frequent myoclonic jerks. At first glance, this phenomenology was more suggestive of a primary hyperkinetic movement disorder than an epileptic encephalopathy. However, the presence of characteristic periodic electroencephalogram (EEG) complexes together with positive measles serology established the diagnosis unequivocally. This observation highlights the crucial role of EEG in the evaluation of children presenting with progressive movement disorders and cognitive decline. In conclusion, this video case illustrates that SSPE is not merely an encephalitic disorder characterized by periodic myoclonus but may also present with a movement disorder-dominant phenotype. Normal brain MRI findings should not exclude the diagnosis. In children presenting with progressive choreoathetoid movements, dystonic posturing, axial instability, and cognitive deterioration, the identification of periodic generalized complexes on EEG should raise strong suspicion of SSPE. In the consent form, the patient provided permission for the use of his clinical information and imaging findings for publication purposes. The patient understands that his name and initials will not be published and that every effort will be made to protect his identity; however, complete anonymity cannot be guaranteed. Ethical approval and consent Written informed consent for publication of the clinical information, neurophysiological data, and video material was obtained from the patient’s legal guardians. Financial support and sponsorship Nil. Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the writing process The authors used Open AI only for language editing, grammar improvement, and manuscript formatting. All clinical information, interpretation, scientific content, and conclusions were independently reviewed and verified by the authors, who accept full responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of the manuscript. Data availability statement Data supporting the findings of this report are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Conflicts of interest There are no conflicts of interest. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the broader clinical spectrum of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), particularly focusing on cases where movement disorders dominate the clinical presentation, challenging diagnostic accuracy. The authors sought to emphasize the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of SSPE, especially in the context of normal brain MRI findings and the critical role of electroencephalography (EEG) in diagnosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a single case report of a 9-year-old boy presenting with progressive gait instability and involuntary movements, initially considered for primary movement disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, or autoimmune encephalitis. The patient underwent clinical evaluation, neurological examination, and electroencephalography (EEG), with MRI showing normal findings. The diagnosis of SSPE was confirmed by elevated anti-measles antibody titers in cerebrospinal fluid and serum.
analysis.methods: The patient was evaluated through clinical assessment, neurological examination, and EEG. MRI was performed to rule out structural abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The patient exhibited progressive cognitive deterioration, behavioral changes, and frequent involuntary movements, including myoclonic jerks and dystonic posturing. EEG revealed characteristic periodic discharges, and elevated anti-measles antibody titers confirmed the SSPE diagnosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of SSPE, particularly when movement disorders dominate the clinical picture. The authors emphasized the critical role of EEG in diagnosing SSPE, even in the absence of typical MRI findings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against excluding SSPE based on normal MRI results and underscore the necessity of considering SSPE in the differential diagnosis of progressive movement disorders and cognitive decline. The study also highlights the importance of EEG in diagnosing SSPE.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single case report design, which does not allow for generalization. However, the findings are supported by characteristic EEG findings and elevated measles-specific antibody titers, providing strong evidence for the diagnosis of SSPE.

analysis.summary_en: This case report highlights the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), particularly when movement disorders dominate the clinical picture. The study emphasizes the critical role of electroencephalography (EEG) in diagnosing SSPE, even in the absence of typical MRI findings.

papers.source_body_en: More recently, a systematic review by Garg et al.[] highlighted the remarkable heterogeneity of movement disorder phenomenology in SSPE and underscored the importance of recognizing atypical presentations. However, involvement of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and cortico-striatal networks is believed to play a central role.[] Neuropathological studies have demonstrated degeneration and inflammatory changes within basal ganglia circuits, which may contribute to the development of hyperkinetic movement disorders.[] Neuroimaging studies have further suggested that thalamic and basal ganglia dysfunction may underlie the emergence of dystonia, chorea, and other abnormal movements.[,] Nevertheless, structural neuroimaging findings may be entirely normal, particularly during the early stages of the disease.[] The absence of MRI abnormalities in our patient likely reflects microscopic pathological changes that remain below the detection threshold of conventional imaging techniques.[] A particularly noteworthy aspect of the present case was the striking predominance of movement disorder manifestations. In conclusion, this video case illustrates that SSPE is not merely an encephalitic disorder characterized by periodic myoclonus but may also present with a movement disorder-dominant phenotype. papers.title: Comparative Modeling of Measles Incidences Among Children Below Five Years in Rivers State, Nigeria Using the Holt-Winters, SARIMA, and Hybrid SARIMA-ANN Models
papers.abstract: This research analyzed various time-series forecasting models for measles occurrences in children younger than five in Rivers State, Nigeria, utilizing monthly data sourced from the Rivers State Hospital Management Board and allied partners spanning from January 2015 to December 2024. Python 3.11 software was used for the data analysis. The investigation focused on the temporal patterns of measles cases and assessed the prediction efficacy of additive Holt–Winters, multiplicative Holt–Winters, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), and hybrid SARIMA–Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models. To explore the data series, methods such as descriptive statistics, seasonal decomposition, the Jarque–Bera normality examination, the Augmented Dickey–Fuller unit-root evaluation, autocorrelation assessment, and the Ljung–Box test were utilized. The forecasting efficiency was measured via root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute scaled error (MASE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Findings indicated an average of 26.17 monthly cases of measles, with a standard deviation of 21.43 and a peak of 124 cases. The data series displayed positive skewness and did not conform to a normal distribution, while the results from the Augmented Dickey–Fuller test suggested stationarity at level significance (p < 0.001). The Ljung–Box analysis uncovered significant serial correlations at lags 12 and 20 (p < 0.001). Out of the four forecasting techniques, the multiplicative Holt–Winters method yielded the best results, achieving the lowest RMSE at 16.43 and a reported MASE of 86.68. Conversely, the hybrid SARIMA–ANN approach was the least effective, presenting an RMSE of 22.05 and a reported MASE of 261.66. The study concludes that the multiplicative Holt–Winters method stands out as the most effective model among those tested. It suggests the validation of the reported MASE values, the importance of consistent out-of-sample evaluation, and enhancing regular measles monitoring to aid in timely forecasting, vaccination strategy, and focused public health actions.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The investigation focused on the temporal patterns of measles cases and assessed the prediction efficacy of four models using monthly data from January 2015 to December 2024. Python 3.11 software was used for the data analysis.
analysis.methods: The data series was explored using descriptive statistics, seasonal decomposition, the Jarque–Bera normality examination, the Augmented Dickey–Fuller unit-root evaluation, autocorrelation assessment, and the Ljung–Box test. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concludes that the multiplicative Holt–Winters method stands out as the most effective model among those tested. papers.title_zh: 使用 Holt-Winters、SARIMA 和混合 SARIMA-ANN 模型对尼日利亚河流州五岁以下儿童的 麻疹 发病率 进行比较建模
papers.source_body_en: This research analyzed various time-series forecasting models for measles occurrences in children younger than five in Rivers State, Nigeria, utilizing monthly data sourced from the Rivers State Hospital Management Board and allied partners spanning from January 2015 to December 2024. Python 3.11 software was used for the data analysis. The investigation focused on the temporal patterns of measles cases and assessed the prediction efficacy of additive Holt–Winters, multiplicative Holt–Winters, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), and hybrid SARIMA–Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models. To explore the data series, methods such as descriptive statistics, seasonal decomposition, the Jarque–Bera normality examination, the Augmented Dickey–Fuller unit-root evaluation, autocorrelation assessment, and the Ljung–Box test were utilized. The forecasting efficiency was measured via root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute scaled error (MASE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Findings indicated an average of 26.17 monthly cases of measles, with a standard deviation of 21.43 and a peak of 124 cases. The data series displayed positive skewness and did not conform to a normal distribution, while the results from the Augmented Dickey–Fuller test suggested stationarity at level significance (p < 0.001). The Ljung–Box analysis uncovered significant serial correlations at lags 12 and 20 (p < 0.001). Out of the four forecasting techniques, the multiplicative Holt–Winters method yielded the best results, achieving the lowest RMSE at 16.43 and a reported MASE of 86.68. Conversely, the hybrid SARIMA–ANN approach was the least effective, presenting an RMSE of 22.05 and a reported MASE of 261.66. The study concludes that the multiplicative Holt–Winters method stands out as the most effective model among those tested. It suggests the validation of the reported MASE values, the importance of consistent out-of-sample evaluation, and enhancing regular measles monitoring to aid in timely forecasting, vaccination strategy, and focused public health actions.

papers.title: The effect of age at first dose of a measles-containing vaccine on measles humoral immunity: a retrospective cohort study, Canada, 2014 to 2016
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Canada eliminated measles in 1998; however, large outbreaks have been recently reported, and elimination status was lost in 2025. AIM We aimed to estimate the effect of age at first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) on measles IgG concentration and seronegativity among two-dose recipients nearly two decades after vaccination. METHODS We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 10,766 twice-vaccinated individuals tested for measles IgG from 2014 to 2016 in Ontario, Canada. We predicted measles IgG concentration and seronegativity using thresholds of RESULTS A 1-month increase in age at MCV1 (between 12 and 15 months) was associated with 13.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 7.1–20.8) higher predicted mean measles IgG concentration for females born after elimination and 9.2% (95% CI: 6.8–11.6) for females born before elimination. Depending on the seronegativity threshold and the measles elimination status at birth, a 1-month increase in age at MCV1 (between 12 and 15 months) was associated with lower odds ratio of seronegativity ranging from 0.74 (95% CI: 0.63–0.85) to 0.87 (95% CI: 0.57–1.27). Using the lowest threshold (≤ 120 mIU/mL) and the longest follow-up period (24 years post-MCV1), we predicted that 4.1% (95% CI: 2.7–6.1) of females vaccinated with MCV1 at 15 months of age would be seronegative, compared with 9.6% (95% CI: 7.4–12.3) of those vaccinated at 12 months. DISCUSSION Delaying MCV1 to older ages (13–15 months) may result in an absolute decrease as large as 6% in the percentage of seronegative individuals, potentially increasing the likelihood of maintaining herd immunity.

papers.title: IMPACTO DA IMUNIZAÇÃO NA ERRADICAÇÃO DO SARAMPO E A INCIDÊNCIA DE SURTOS EPIDEMIOLÓGICOS NO BRASIL EM 2025 THE IMPACT OF IMMUNIZATION ON MEASLES ERADICATION AND THE INCIDENCE OF EPIDEMIOLOGICAL OUTBREAKS IN BRAZIL IN 2025 EL IMPACTO DE LA INMUNIZACIÓN EN LA ERRADICACIÓN DEL SARAMPIÓN Y LA INCIDENCIA DE BROTES EPIDEMIOLÓGICOS EN BRASIL EN 2025
papers.abstract: Este artigo buscou analisar o impacto da imunização no controle e na eliminação do sarampo, relacionando a cobertura vacinal à incidência de surtos epidemiológicos no Brasil, com ênfase no cenário observado em 2025. Trata-se de um estudo epidemiológico descritivo, retrospectivo e de abordagem quantitativa, fundamentado em dados secundários provenientes de sistemas oficiais de vigilância em saúde e imunização, considerando registros do período de 2020 a 2025. Foram analisadas informações referentes aos casos confirmados, cobertura vacinal, distribuição temporal e ocorrência de surtos, com destaque para o estado do Tocantins. Os dados demonstraram redução expressiva dos casos após 2021, ausência de confirmações em 2023 e posterior ocorrência de novos registros em 2024 e 2025. Em 2025, destacou-se o surto ocorrido no município de Campos Lindos, no Tocantins, associado à introdução do vírus após viagem internacional e à presença de indivíduos suscetíveis. Os achados reforçam que a vacinação constitui a principal estratégia para interromper a transmissão do sarampo. Conclui-se que a manutenção de elevada e homogênea cobertura vacinal, associada à vigilância epidemiológica contínua, é indispensável para prevenir novos surtos e sustentar a eliminação da doença no Brasil.

source_records.abstract: Este artigo buscou analisar o impacto da imunização no controle e na eliminação do sarampo, relacionando a cobertura vacinal à incidência de surtos epidemiológicos no Brasil, com ênfase no cenário observado em 2025. Trata-se de um estudo epidemiológico descritivo, retrospectivo e de abordagem quantitativa, fundamentado em dados secundários provenientes de sistemas oficiais de vigilância em saúde e imunização, considerando registros do período de 2020 a 2025. Foram analisadas informações referentes aos casos confirmados, cobertura vacinal, distribuição temporal e ocorrência de surtos, com destaque para o estado do Tocantins. Os dados demonstraram redução expressiva dos casos após 2021, ausência de confirmações em 2023 e posterior ocorrência de novos registros em 2024 e 2025. Em 2025, destacou-se o surto ocorrido no município de Campos Lindos, no Tocantins, associado à introdução do vírus após viagem internacional e à presença de indivíduos suscetíveis. Os achados reforçam que a vacinação constitui a principal estratégia para interromper a transmissão do sarampo. Conclui-se que a manutenção de elevada e homogênea cobertura vacinal, associada à vigilância epidemiológica contínua, é indispensável para prevenir novos surtos e sustentar a eliminação da doença no Brasil.

papers.title: Project 004: code and reproduction package for loss of measles elimination and a century of post-control resurgence
papers.abstract: Code, records and derived tables of the study "Loss of measles elimination and a century of post-control resurgence" (Boyuan Wang, Shangkun Zhong, Le Yu, Xueqian Yi; Zhuhai Fudan Innovation Research Institute). Preregistration 2: https://osf.io/a4y2x; rapid preregistration: https://osf.io/xtwjc. The package keeps the project's folder layout, so every path in the registrations and in the lock records can be checked as written. It holds the code, data manifests (no third-party raw data), lock records with RFC 3161 time stamps, confirmatory outputs, derived tables, smoke tests and a script that recomputes the main result; see README.md in the package. Licence ("Other"): the terms are those of the licence files in the package. Code: MIT (LICENSE). Documentation, records and data summaries: CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-docs.md). Values derived from WHO data remain under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, and values derived from CShapes 2.0, the Global Transnational Mobility dataset and OpenFlights keep the terms of their sources (LICENSE-docs.md, DERIVED_TABLES.tsv). How to cite: CITATION.cff.

analysis.main_results: The package contains the code, data summaries, and derived tables necessary to reproduce the main results of the study on measles elimination and post-control resurgence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors state that the package provides a transparent and reproducible framework for analyzing the historical patterns of measles elimination and resurgence, which is novel in its approach to data and code sharing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for measles control and surveillance by providing a reproducible method to analyze historical data and model disease resurgence.

analysis.summary_en: This preprint provides a code and reproduction package for analyzing the loss of measles elimination and a century of post-control resurgence. The study aims to understand the historical patterns of measles disease control and resurgence, using a transparent and reproducible framework. The methods include a code package with data manifests, lock records, confirmatory outputs, derived tables, and a script to recompute the main result. The main results are the code, data summaries, and derived tables necessary for the analysis. The authors interpret these findings as a novel approach to data and code sharing, which can inform public health strategies for measles surveillance and control. However, the study is limited to providing documentation and code rather than direct empirical results, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一份预印本,提供了用于分析 麻疹 消除和控制后复苏的代码、记录和派生表格,摘要中没有提供具体的人群详细信息。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及使用代码包,其中包括数据清单、带有 RFC 3161 时间戳的锁定记录、确认输出、派生表、冒烟测试以及用于重新计算主要结果的脚本,如 README.md 文件中详述。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该软件包包含重现 麻疹 消除和控制后复苏研究主要结果所需的代码、数据摘要和派生表格。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者表示,该软件包提供了一个透明且可重复的框架,用于分析 麻疹 消除和复兴的历史模式,其数据和代码共享方法是新颖的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过提供一种可重复的方法来分析历史数据和模拟疾病复发,这些发现可以为 麻疹 控制和 监测 的公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于提供代码和文档,而不是直接的实证结果,并且由于所提供的信息仅具有抽象性质,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Loss of measles elimination in a century of post-control resurgence: full preregistration of confirmatory analyses (preregistration 2 of 2)
papers.abstract: This is the second of two preregistrations of one project (preregistration 1: https://osf.io/xtwjc). It registers, before any confirmatory analysis is run, the hypotheses with their support and refutation criteria, the frozen code and configuration files identified by SHA-256 hashes and timestamped lock records, the configurations selected by two pre-registered model searches, the decision rules and the evidence gate, and the sealing of the test period 2023–2026. Part A asks whether the amplitude and the onset hazard of resurgence after control of immunisable diseases follow a common law driven by the accumulation of susceptible births (C1). Part B builds a lead-time-stratified risk assessment of loss of measles elimination status (H1), examines adult immunity gaps (H2) and importation pressure (H3), and places the 2025–26 measles resurgence in the United States within a century of post-control resurgences (H4). All development used data up to 31 December 2022. Test-period performance has not been computed for any analysis, and the code refuses to compute it until this registration has an OSF registration number. Deviations registered before registration (DV01–DV19), prior data access and the addenda to be posted after registration are listed in the text.

papers.title: Association between residence in flood-prone areas and incomplete childhood vaccination in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Flooding events, closely linked to climate change and variability, can disrupt communities and health systems. Vaccination, a highly effective public health intervention, plays a crucial role in preventing child mortality worldwide. However, the relationship between flood-prone residence and early childhood vaccination remains underexplored. This study combines flood exposure data from the Global Flood Database with five waves of Demographic and Health Surveys (2004-2018) in Bangladesh, including vaccination histories for children under three years. Using geographic coordinates, households were matched to spatial flood data to identify whether children lived in flood-prone areas. Generalized Estimating Equations were applied, accounting for geographic clustering, to assess the association between flood exposure and incomplete vaccination overall, as well as by vaccine type and dose. The total sample included 19,021 children, with 12,930 of them being over 1 years old and included in the main analysis. Of those over one year, 16% were defined as living in flood-prone areas, and 84% were fully vaccinated. Children in flood-prone areas had a higher risk of missing the diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis (DTP; PR = 1.34, CI: 1.11-1.62) vaccine, the bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG; PR = 1.24, CI: 1.02-1.50) vaccine, and the oral polio vaccine (OPV; PR = 1.32, CI: 1.10-1.59) vaccines. Associations were not precise for the measles-containing vaccine (MCV; PR = 1.11, CI: 0.92-1.35) alone, nor for all four vaccines combined (PR = 1.09, CI: 0.91-1.30). These findings highlight that there is an association between residence in flood prone areas and certain vaccines, highlighting the importance of maintaining access to routine immunization services during floods, which are expected to increase with climate change.

papers.title: Strengthening catch-up vaccination delivery in routine health services for children under five in Western Kenya, 2022-2024.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Catch-up vaccination can close population immunity gaps, yet integration into routine immunization services remains limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Following Kenya's 2023 catch-up vaccination policy, we evaluated a multi-strategy intervention to strengthen systematic identification, eligibility screening, and delivery of missed doses within routine health services in Siaya County. METHODS: Over 12 months, five strategies addressing healthcare worker (HCW) capacity, vaccination documentation, defaulter tracking, immunization screening, and caregiver engagement were implemented in 55 public health facilities selected through stratified random sampling. Using a pre-post design, we assessed immunization uptake, missed opportunities for vaccination (MOVs), and system readiness. Baseline (November 2022-January 2023) and endline (October-December 2024) evaluations included facility assessments, HCW interviews, caregiver exit surveys among children aged <36 months with home-based records (HBRs; n = 658), and facility immunization register abstractions (n = 1650 children aged 12-23 months). Analyses accounted for sampling design, clustering, and used generalized estimating equations for HBR data. RESULTS: MOV prevalence among children visiting facilities for any reason declined from 94.4% to 20.9% (p < 0.001). Full immunization among children aged 12-23 months increased from 44.9% to 63.6% (p < 0.001), with uptake improving across antigens. Measles-rubella first-dose uptake increased from 51.5% to 78.0%, and second-dose uptake from 18.8% to 36.9% (p < 0.001 for both). Eligibility screening expanded from 60.6% to 86.8% of facilities (p = 0.012), defaulter tracking improved from 48.5% to 91.6% (p < 0.001), and HCW knowledge and confidence increased significantly. CONCLUSION: The multi-strategy intervention was associated with fewer MOVs and improved uptake, suggesting that embedding catch-up vaccination within routine health services can strengthen immunization systems in decentralized LMIC contexts. Kenya's catch-up vaccination policy provided a framework for introducing catch-up vaccination into routine health services.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:追赶 疫苗接种 可以缩小人群免疫差距,但在低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC),融入常规免疫服务仍然有限。根据肯尼亚的 2023 年 疫苗接种 追赶政策,我们评估了一项多策略干预措施,以加强西亚县常规卫生服务中的系统识别、资格筛查和漏服剂量的提供。方法:在 12 个月的时间里,在通过分层随机抽样选出的 55 个公共卫生机构中实施了五项策略,涉及医疗保健工作者 (HCW) 能力、疫苗接种 文档、违约者跟踪、免疫筛查和护理人员参与。使用前后设计,我们评估了免疫接种率、疫苗接种 (MOV) 错过的机会以及系统准备情况。基线(2022 年 11 月至 2023 年 1 月)和终点(2024 年 10 月至 12 月)评估包括设施评估、医护人员访谈、对年龄 < 36 个月的儿童进行的护理人员退出调查(HBR;n = 658)以及设施免疫登记摘要(n = 1650 名 12-23 个月的儿童)。分析考虑了抽样设计、聚类,并使用了 HBR 数据的广义估计方程。结果:出于任何原因访问设施的儿童中 MOV 患病率 从 94.4% 下降至 20.9% (p < 0.001)。12-23 个月龄儿童的完全免疫率从 44.9% 增加到 63.6% (p < 0.001),各种抗原的吸收率有所提高。麻疹-风疹第一剂吸收率从 51.5% 增加到 78.0%,第二剂吸收率从 18.8% 增加到 36.9%(两者的 p < 0.001)。设施的资格筛查从 60.6% 扩大到 86.8% (p = 0.012),违约者跟踪从 48.5% 提高到 91.6% (p < 0.001),医护人员的知识和信心显着增加。结论:多策略干预与较少的 MOV 和提高的吸收率相关,这表明将追赶型 疫苗接种 纳入常规卫生服务可以加强分散的中低收入国家的免疫系统。肯尼亚的追赶型 疫苗接种 政策为将追赶型 疫苗接种 引入常规卫生服务提供了框架。

papers.title: Microarray patches for transdermal drug delivery: a critical narrative review of technological innovations, CMC challenges, clinical translation, and global health implementation
papers.abstract: Microarray patches (MAPs), alternatively known as microneedle patches, is a paradigm shift in the administration of pharmaceutical agents and vaccines. By utilising micron-scale projections to breach the stratum corneum, MAPs bridge the gap between the convenience of transdermal patches and the efficacy of hypodermic injections. This critical narrative review synthesises advances in MAP technology for transdermal drug delivery, focusing on technological innovations, chemistry, manufacturing, and control (CMC) challenges, clinical translation, regulatory considerations, and global health implementation. Special emphasis is placed on CMC challenges, including sterilisation and stability profiling, as well as the landscape of Clinical Trials, highlighting recent frameworks for pivotal Phase III studies in measles and rubella. We conclude by evaluating the programmatic suitability of MAPs for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), addressing critical barriers such as cold-chain logistics and trypanophobia. A coordinated evolution from product-by-product model to platform-industrialisation model involving vaccine, polymer and device producing companies, regulators, global-health agencies including World health organization (WHO), and technology enablers is necessary. The Measles-Rubella programme provides an important template. MAPs’ value is not about replacing a syringe but enabling equitable distribution of vaccination; a strategy to make vaccination less dependent on infrastructure. As scientific innovations, upscaling, unified regulatory frameworks and equitable access advance, MAPs will achieve global relevance.

papers.title: Bridging microbiology and public health through simulation-based learning.
papers.abstract: Within our synchronous, online global health-focused upper-level microbiology course, we find that students struggle to translate learning to real-world applications. For example, consider the recent measles outbreaks and major events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, which prompt many questions about how basic microbiological information is used by public health professionals. To address these points, we created a simulation-based curriculum that places students in an action role during an infectious disease outbreak. Our stand-alone curriculum walks through a historical measles outbreak that introduces outbreak investigation, community communication, and how these depend on microbiological knowledge. By using breakout groups, students have an opportunity to decide classifications, public messaging, and intervention metrics. We provide students with an outbreak investigation reference worksheet and interweave breakout rooms with didactic vignettes covering background information while revealing actual responses to outbreaks in conjunction with data obtained by responding scientists. Students synthesize material and apply it in real-time, allowing them to exercise critical thinking. Pilot testing in a small, upper-division, virtual classroom suggests that this curriculum has strong potential for increasing mastery of learning objectives and bolstering the relevance of microbiology and public health to popular media.
papers.journal: Journal of Microbiology and Biology Education

papers.title: Discrete dynamic survival analysis of epidemic case line lists
papers.abstract: Case line lists, which record dates of onset, recovery, and hospitalisation, are among the most granular data in infectious disease epidemiology and can provide insights into transmission dynamics. Dynamic survival analysis (DSA) fits a deterministic, differential-equation-based model to line lists to estimate parameters such as infectivity and the infectious period. Infectious periods are usually not exponential, and incorporating this into mechanistic models for line-list data often requires partial differential equation (PDE) schemes that can be difficult to implement and must be customised for each model, which may limit their use. Here, we propose Discrete Dynamic Survival Analysis (DDSA), a discrete-time DSA for case line lists based on difference equations. It matches calendar-day data directly without interpolation, and its log-likelihood is differentiable via forward-mode automatic differentiation, enabling off-the-shelf gradient-based samplers without model-specific numerical infrastructure. Non-exponential infectious periods are accommodated through a boxcar model or a discrete analogue of the "device of stages". We apply the DDSA method to three historical outbreaks of influenza A(H1N1), Ebola, and measles. DDSA estimates of transmission parameters were close to published analyses where these were available, an agreement that partly reflects shared modelling choices, and the method handles incomplete line lists with missing onset or recovery dates. Synthetic experiments show that recovery intervals identify the infectious period, while infection times and final size constrain R0 when the population at risk is known. Discrete DSA provides a simple, extensible framework for simulation and inference of infectious disease dynamics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决动态生存分析(DSA)在处理离散时间数据和非指数传染期方面的局限性,这在传染病 流行病学 中很常见。病例列表记录了发病、康复和住院日期,是传染病 流行病学 中最精细的数据之一,可以提供对 传播 动态的深入了解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将离散动态生存分析(DDSA)应用于甲型H1N1流感、埃博拉病毒和麻疹的三个历史麻疹。DDSA 是一种基于差分方程的案例行列表的离散时间 DSA,它直接匹配日历日数据,无需插值。
elements_zh.methods: 传播 参数的 DDSA 估计值接近于已发布的可用分析,这一协议部分反映了共享的建模选择,并且该方法处理缺少发病或恢复日期的不完整行列表。综合实验表明,恢复间隔确定了感染期,而当已知危险人群时,感染时间和最终规模限制了 R0。
elements_zh.main_results: 传播 参数的 DDSA 估计值接近已发布的可用分析,并且该方法可以处理缺少发病或恢复日期的不完整行列表。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,DDSA 为传染病动态的模拟和推理提供了一个简单、可扩展的框架,它可以通过棚车模型或“阶段设备”的离散模拟来适应非指数传染期。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DDSA可以洞察传播的动态并处理不完整的线表,这对于传染病的监测、诊断和治疗具有重要意义。该方法可以应用于各种历史麻疹,包括麻疹。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括该方法的性能是根据历史 暴发 进行评估的,并且它可能无法很好地推广到其他疾病或环境。由于证据仅具有抽象性质,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Retrospective Analysis of the VAERS Database for Children One Year of Age
papers.abstract: In recent studies, novel candidate safety signals were detected for infants younger than 1 year of age for specific vaccines. Herein, the Vaccine Adverse Events Reporting System (VAERS) database was retrospectively examined for possible novel candidate safety signals for children one year of age. Novel candidate safety signals were detected for multiple vaccines. Two candidate manufacturing irregularities or possible unknown contaminants were identified associated with adverse event (AE) autism for VAERS nondomestic Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR II) vaccine lots from 1993 to 1995 and AE hyperpyrexia for nondomestic MMRV lots from 2019 to 2024. The candidate manufacturing irregularities were named alpha for MMR II and beta for Measles, Mumps, Rubella, and Varicella (MMRV) ProQuad vaccines. The hypothesized higher levels of alpha in the nondomestic data, MMR II appear to have been reduced or eliminated sometime soon after 1995; identification of alpha would contribute to future avoidance of possible associated AEs. Reduction of beta in the nondomestic MMRV vaccine is hypothesized to reduce hyperpyrexia and also higher pyrexia AEs not observed associated with domestic MMRV vaccine.

papers.title: Advancements in oncolytic virus therapy: a new horizon for ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, and the limited durability of standard treatments has motivated the development of new therapeutic strategies. Oncolytic viruses selectively replicate within and lyse tumor cells, releasing tumor antigens and inflammatory signals that can convert an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment into an immune-inflamed state. This review evaluates the principal platforms used in ovarian cancer, including adenovirus, reovirus, measles virus, vaccinia virus, herpes simplex virus, and vesicular stomatitis virus. We compare engineering approaches that enhance tumor-selective replication, cellular entry, transgene delivery, and local immune activation, and discuss strategies to overcome neutralizing antibodies, restricted intratumoral spread, off-target toxicity, and tumor heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on cytokine- or bispecific T-cell engager-armed viruses and their combination with chemotherapy, immune checkpoint blockade, and cellular immunotherapy. Early-phase studies support the feasibility of intraperitoneal delivery, whereas a single-arm phase 2 study of Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy reported encouraging results, and a randomized phase 3 trial is ongoing. No oncolytic viruses have been approved for ovarian cancer; however, current evidence supports biomarker-guided and rationally sequenced clinical development.

papers.title_zh: 溶瘤病毒治疗的进展:卵巢癌的新视野
papers.source_body_en: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, and the limited durability of standard treatments has motivated the development of new therapeutic strategies. Oncolytic viruses selectively replicate within and lyse tumor cells, releasing tumor antigens and inflammatory signals that can convert an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment into an immune-inflamed state. This review evaluates the principal platforms used in ovarian cancer, including adenovirus, reovirus, measles virus, vaccinia virus, herpes simplex virus, and vesicular stomatitis virus. We compare engineering approaches that enhance tumor-selective replication, cellular entry, transgene delivery, and local immune activation, and discuss strategies to overcome neutralizing antibodies, restricted intratumoral spread, off-target toxicity, and tumor heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on cytokine- or bispecific T-cell engager-armed viruses and their combination with chemotherapy, immune checkpoint blockade, and cellular immunotherapy. Early-phase studies support the feasibility of intraperitoneal delivery, whereas a single-arm phase 2 study of Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy reported encouraging results, and a randomized phase 3 trial is ongoing. No oncolytic viruses have been approved for ovarian cancer; however, current evidence supports biomarker-guided and rationally sequenced clinical development.
papers.abstract_zh: 卵巢癌仍然是最致命的妇科恶性肿瘤,标准 治疗 有限的耐久性促进了新治疗策略的开发。溶瘤病毒选择性地在肿瘤细胞内复制并裂解肿瘤细胞,释放肿瘤抗原和炎症信号,从而将免疫抑制的肿瘤微环境转变为免疫炎症状态。本综述评估了卵巢癌中使用的主要平台,包括腺病毒、呼肠孤病毒、麻疹病毒、牛痘病毒、单纯疱疹病毒和水泡性口炎病毒。我们比较了增强肿瘤选择性复制、细胞进入、转基因递送和局部免疫激活的工程方法,并讨论了克服中和抗体、有限的瘤内扩散、脱靶毒性和肿瘤异质性的策略。特别强调细胞因子或双特异性 T 细胞接合病毒及其与化疗、免疫检查点阻断和细胞免疫疗法的组合。早期研究支持腹腔内给药的可行性,而 Olvi-Vec 的单臂 2 期研究随后进行铂类化疗报告了令人鼓舞的结果,并且随机 3 期试验正在进行中。尚无溶瘤病毒被批准用于治疗卵巢癌;然而,目前的证据支持生物标志物指导和合理排序的临床开发。

papers.title: Travelers and Human–Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases
papers.abstract: Background: International travel can accelerate the geographic spread of zoonotic pathogens and, under certain circumstances, contribute to epidemic or pandemic dissemination. Travelers may also transmit human pathogens to wildlife at tourism interfaces, acting as intermediaries in zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. Methods: Archived WHO and ECDC reports were screened for major zoonotic outbreaks in which international travel contributed to cross-border spread. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies of human-to-wildlife transmission involving tourists, visitors, or travelers and traveler behaviors that could facilitate transmission. Results: Among 14 major zoonotic outbreaks, travelers commonly acted as spreaders following initial animal-to-human spillover by importing infections into new regions, sometimes resulting in onward transmission. This pattern was prominent with respiratory infections such as SARS, MERS, influenza, and COVID-19 and vector-borne infections such as Oropouche and Zika. Twenty-one studies reported possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human–wildlife tourism interfaces. Pathogens included respiratory viruses, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, enteric pathogens, and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Affected wildlife included great apes, primates, elephants, felines, carnivorans, ungulates, avians, reptiles, and urban-adapted wildlife in national parks, zoological parks, rehabilitation centers, and semi-urban parks. Five additional studies documented risky tourist behaviors, including close approach to, physical contact with, and feeding and visiting wildlife while having respiratory symptoms, and inadequate vaccination against measles, influenza, and polio. Conclusions: Travelers can influence transmission bidirectionally by disseminating zoonotic pathogens and exposing wildlife to human pathogens. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization alongside conventional traveler protection.

papers.title_original: Travelers and Human–Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of travelers in the transmission of zoonotic and reverse zoonotic diseases, with a focus on the measles virus. It explores how international travel can facilitate the spread of pathogens between humans and animals, and how human behaviors at wildlife interfaces may contribute to the transmission of human pathogens to wildlife.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilized archived WHO and ECDC reports to identify major zoonotic outbreaks involving international travel. It also conducted searches on PubMed and Scopus for studies on human-to-wildlife transmission and traveler behaviors that could facilitate such transmission.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Travelers can act as intermediaries in both zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. They commonly import infections into new regions following initial animal-to-human spillover, which can lead to onward transmission. This pattern is particularly evident with respiratory infections such as measles, influenza, and others.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is evidence of travelers spreading zoonotic pathogens, the mechanisms and extent of reverse zoonotic transmission remain underexplored. Additionally, the role of specific behaviors, such as feeding wildlife or inadequate vaccination, in facilitating transmission is not fully quantified.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a need for targeted research on the role of traveler behaviors in reverse zoonotic transmission. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization to mitigate risks.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the bidirectional transmission of zoonotic and reverse zoonotic diseases involving travelers, with a focus on the measles virus. It highlights how international travel can accelerate the spread of pathogens between humans and animals, particularly respiratory viruses. The review identifies 14 major zoonotic outbreaks where travelers played a role in spreading infections, and 21 studies report possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human-wildlife interfaces. The review emphasizes the need for travel medicine to include wildlife-protective measures, such as hygiene and immunization, to reduce transmission risks. However, the mechanisms and extent of reverse zoonotic transmission remain underexplored, and further research is needed to address these gaps.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了旅行者在人畜共患疾病和反向人畜共患疾病 传播 中的作用,重点是 麻疹病毒。它探讨了国际旅行如何促进病原体在人类和动物之间的传播,以及人类在野生动物接触面的行为如何可能导致人类病原体传播给野生动物。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查利用世卫组织和欧洲疾病预防控制中心存档的报告来确定涉及国际旅行的主要人畜共患病 暴发。它还在 PubMed 和 Scopus 上搜索有关人类与野生动物 传播 以及可能促进此类 传播 的旅行者行为的研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 旅行者可以充当人畜共患病和反向人畜共患病 传播 的中介人。它们通常在最初的动物到人类 跨物种溢出 后将感染引入新区域,这可能导致后续的 传播。这种模式在 麻疹、流感等呼吸道感染中尤其明显。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然有证据表明旅行者传播人畜共患病原体,但反向人畜共患 传播 的机制和程度仍未得到充分研究。此外,特定行为(例如喂养野生动物或 疫苗接种 不足)在促进 传播 中的作用尚未完全量化。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of travelers in the transmission of zoonotic and reverse zoonotic diseases, with a focus on the measles virus. It explores how international travel can facilitate the spread of pathogens between humans and animals, and how human behaviors at wildlife interfaces may contribute to the transmission of human pathogens to wildlife.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilized archived WHO and ECDC reports to identify major zoonotic outbreaks involving international travel. It also conducted searches on PubMed and Scopus for studies on human-to-wildlife transmission and traveler behaviors that could facilitate such transmission.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Travelers can act as intermediaries in both zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. They commonly import infections into new regions following initial animal-to-human spillover, which can lead to onward transmission. This pattern is particularly evident with respiratory infections such as measles, influenza, and others.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is evidence of travelers spreading zoonotic pathogens, the mechanisms and extent of reverse zoonotic transmission remain underexplored. Additionally, the role of specific behaviors, such as feeding wildlife or inadequate vaccination, in facilitating transmission is not fully quantified.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: There is a need for targeted research on the role of traveler behaviors in reverse zoonotic transmission. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization to mitigate risks.

papers.title_zh: 旅行者和人畜病原体 传播:人畜共患病和反向人畜共患疾病的一次健康回顾
papers.source_body_en: Background: International travel can accelerate the geographic spread of zoonotic pathogens and, under certain circumstances, contribute to epidemic or pandemic dissemination. Travelers may also transmit human pathogens to wildlife at tourism interfaces, acting as intermediaries in zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. Methods: Archived WHO and ECDC reports were screened for major zoonotic outbreaks in which international travel contributed to cross-border spread. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies of human-to-wildlife transmission involving tourists, visitors, or travelers and traveler behaviors that could facilitate transmission. Results: Among 14 major zoonotic outbreaks, travelers commonly acted as spreaders following initial animal-to-human spillover by importing infections into new regions, sometimes resulting in onward transmission. This pattern was prominent with respiratory infections such as SARS, MERS, influenza, and COVID-19 and vector-borne infections such as Oropouche and Zika. Twenty-one studies reported possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human–wildlife tourism interfaces. Pathogens included respiratory viruses, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, enteric pathogens, and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Affected wildlife included great apes, primates, elephants, felines, carnivorans, ungulates, avians, reptiles, and urban-adapted wildlife in national parks, zoological parks, rehabilitation centers, and semi-urban parks. Five additional studies documented risky tourist behaviors, including close approach to, physical contact with, and feeding and visiting wildlife while having respiratory symptoms, and inadequate vaccination against measles, influenza, and polio. Conclusions: Travelers can influence transmission bidirectionally by disseminating zoonotic pathogens and exposing wildlife to human pathogens. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization alongside conventional traveler protection.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:国际旅行可以加速人畜共患病病原体的地理传播,并在某些情况下导致流行病或大流行的传播。旅行者还可能在旅游界面将人类病原体传播给野生动物,充当人畜共患和反向人畜共患 传播 的中介。方法:对存档的 WHO 和 ECDC 报告进行了筛查,以了解主要人畜共患病 暴发,其中国际旅行导致了跨境传播。在 PubMed 和 Scopus 中检索了有关人类与野生动物 传播 的研究,其中涉及游客、访客或可能促进 传播 的旅行者和旅行者行为。结果:在 14 种主要人畜共患 暴发 中,旅行者通常在最初的动物到人类 跨物种溢出 后充当传播者,将感染引入新地区,有时会导致进一步的 传播。这种模式在 SARS、MERS、流感和 COVID-19 等呼吸道感染以及 Oropouche 和 Zika 等 媒介 传播的感染中尤为突出。二十一项研究报告了人类与野生动物旅游界面可能或证实的反向人畜共患 传播。病原体包括呼吸道病毒、结核分枝杆菌、肠道病原体和耐药病原体。受影响的野生动物包括类人猿、灵长类动物、大象、猫科动物、食肉动物、有蹄类动物、鸟类、爬行动物以及国家公园、动物园、康复中心和半城市公园中适应城市的野生动物。另外五项研究记录了危险的游客行为,包括在出现呼吸道症状时近距离接近、身体接触、喂养和参观野生动物,以及针对 麻疹、流感和脊髓灰质炎的 麻疹 不足。结论:旅行者可以通过传播人畜共患病原体并使野生动物接触人类病原体来双向影响 传播。旅行医学应将有关距离、卫生、废物处理和免疫接种的野生动物保护咨询与传统的旅行者保护结合起来。

papers.title: Comparison of routine health-facility (KHIS) versus house-survey (KDHS) estimates of childhood vaccination coverage in Kenya: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reliable estimates of effective coverage of health interventions are essential for tracking progress towards health goals and informing policy decisions. In settings where routine health information systems are limited, population-based household surveys are frequently used as reference standards. OBJECTIVE: This study compared national and sub-national childhood vaccination coverage estimates from Kenya's facility-based Health Information System (KHIS) and the 2022 Kenya Demographic Health Survey (KDHS) to assess concordance between the two data sources and to evaluate the suitability of routine data for programmatic decision-making. METHODS: We analysed BCG, pentavalent 1, pentavalent 3 and measles-rubella 1 (MR 1) vaccination data reported by 8178 health facilities to KHIS between March 2020 and March 2022 alongside KDHS 2022 data from 3679 children aged 12-23 months. Coverage estimates were compared at national and county levels using a two-proportion z-test. Absolute differences in coverage were categorised as minimal ( 10%) occurred in 9-14 counties. Only three counties showed absolute differences <5% across all four antigens; several counties showed persistent divergence across antigens. CONCLUSION: KHIS yields reasonably concordant national-level estimates of childhood vaccination coverage, but substantial and uneven county-level discrepancies limit its reliability for sub-national decision-making. A differentiated approach is warranted: KHIS can support national trend monitoring and may be usable in counties with demonstrated concordance, whereas counties with persistent divergence require continued survey-based validation and targeted strengthening of routine data systems. The two data sources should not be treated as interchangeable at county level.

Reliable estimates of effective coverage of health interventions are essential for tracking progress towards health goals and informing policy decisions, especially in settings where routine health information systems are limited, and population-based household surveys are frequently used as reference standards.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared national and sub-national childhood vaccination coverage estimates from KHIS and KDHS 2022 data from 3679 children aged 12-23 months. The analysis included BCG, pentavalent 1, pentavalent 3, and measles-rubella 1 (MR 1) vaccination data reported by 8178 health facilities to KHIS between March 2020 and March 2022.
analysis.methods: Coverage estimates were compared at national and county levels using a two-proportion z-test. Absolute differences in coverage were categorised as minimal (≤5%) or substantial (>5%).
analysis.main_results: Only three counties showed absolute differences <5% across all four antigens; several counties showed persistent divergence across antigens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在比较肯尼亚基于设施的健康信息系统 (KHIS) 和 2022 年肯尼亚人口健康调查 (KDHS) 的国家和次国家儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值,以评估两个数据源之间的一致性,并评估常规数据对规划决策的适用性。对健康干预措施有效覆盖范围的可靠估计对于跟踪健康目标的进展情况和为政策决策提供信息至关重要,特别是在常规卫生信息系统有限且经常使用基于人口的家庭调查作为参考标准的环境中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了来自 3679 名 12-23 个月儿童的 KHIS 和 KDHS 2022 数据的国家和次国家儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值。该分析包括 2020 年 3 月至 2022 年 3 月期间 8178 个卫生机构向 KHIS 报告的 BCG、五价 1、五价 3 和 麻疹-风疹 1 (MR 1) 疫苗接种 数据。
elements_zh.methods: 使用二比例 z 检验在国家和县一级比较覆盖率估计值。覆盖率的绝对差异分为最小(≤5%)或显着(>5%)。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有三个县的所有四种抗原的绝对差异<5%;几个县的抗原表现出持续的差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: KHIS 得出了相当一致的国家级儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值,但县级的巨大且不均匀的差异限制了其在地方决策中的可靠性。需要采取差异化的方法:KHIS 可以支持国家趋势监测,并且可用于具有一致性的县,而持续存在差异的县则需要继续基于调查的验证并有针对性地加强常规数据系统。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,虽然 KHIS 可以提供可靠的国家级估计,但未经进一步验证,它不适合地方决策。这对 疫苗 可预防疾病的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 具有影响,特别是与 ZX​​QTERMEQXZ 密切相关的 麻疹。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括潜在的偏差和混杂因素,以及样本量和普遍性。由于研究设计的局限性以及需要在存在持续分歧的县进行进一步验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 肯尼亚儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率的常规卫生设施 (KHIS) 与房屋调查 (KDHS) 估计值的比较:一项横断面研究。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Reliable estimates of effective coverage of health interventions are essential for tracking progress towards health goals and informing policy decisions. In settings where routine health information systems are limited, population-based household surveys are frequently used as reference standards. OBJECTIVE: This study compared national and sub-national childhood vaccination coverage estimates from Kenya's facility-based Health Information System (KHIS) and the 2022 Kenya Demographic Health Survey (KDHS) to assess concordance between the two data sources and to evaluate the suitability of routine data for programmatic decision-making. METHODS: We analysed BCG, pentavalent 1, pentavalent 3 and measles-rubella 1 (MR 1) vaccination data reported by 8178 health facilities to KHIS between March 2020 and March 2022 alongside KDHS 2022 data from 3679 children aged 12-23 months. Coverage estimates were compared at national and county levels using a two-proportion z-test. Absolute differences in coverage were categorised as minimal ( 10%) occurred in 9-14 counties. Only three counties showed absolute differences <5% across all four antigens; several counties showed persistent divergence across antigens. CONCLUSION: KHIS yields reasonably concordant national-level estimates of childhood vaccination coverage, but substantial and uneven county-level discrepancies limit its reliability for sub-national decision-making. A differentiated approach is warranted: KHIS can support national trend monitoring and may be usable in counties with demonstrated concordance, whereas counties with persistent divergence require continued survey-based validation and targeted strengthening of routine data systems. The two data sources should not be treated as interchangeable at county level.

papers.title: Could Microarray Patch Vaccines Contribute to Pandemic Preparedness? Opportunities, Implementation Considerations, and Priorities
papers.abstract: Microarray patches (MAPs) demonstrate potential to improve pandemic preparedness by supporting rapid and large-scale vaccine distribution and administration, particularly in settings with limited cold-chain capacity or health workforce resources. This narrative review synthesises preclinical and clinical MAP vaccine research alongside literature on product development, manufacturing, regulation, implementation, acceptability, and equitable access, and reports encouraging early-phase tolerability and immunogenicity findings for influenza, Japanese encephalitis, measles–rubella, and SARS-CoV-2 MAP vaccines. Notable advantages include improved thermostability, antigen dose sparing, simplified application, the possibility of self- or layperson administration, reduced reliance on trained vaccinators, and suitability for outreach and low-resource settings. Advancing MAP technology requires selection of target vaccines, development of stable, antigen-specific formulations, confirmation of dose delivery, completion of phased clinical trials and regulatory assessments, establishment of scalable, quality-controlled manufacturing systems, and integration into immunization programmes. Challenges involve antigen compatibility, dose consistency, formulation stability, manufacturing scale-up, regulatory requirements, uncertain costs and commercial incentives, public acceptance, and equitable access. Following licensure, Phase IV surveillance and effectiveness studies will be needed to evaluate real-world safety and performance. Investment across research, manufacturing, regulation, and delivery is essential to position MAPs as complementary tools to conventional vaccines, thus broadening the speed, reach, and flexibility of pandemic immunization responses.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了微阵列贴片 (MAP) 疫苗 在加强大流行防范方面的潜力,重点是 麻疹病毒。核心问题是 MAP 是否可以改善 疫苗 的分配和管理,特别是在冷链能力或卫生劳动力资源有限的资源匮乏环境中。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 获得许可后,审查建议需要进行 IV 期 监测 和有效性研究,以评估现实世界的安全性和性能。跨研究、制造、监管和交付的投资对于将 MAP 定位为传统 疫苗 的补充工具至关重要。

papers.full_text: 659 Editorial EMHJ – Vol. 32 No. 10 – 2026 After Regional Committee 73, what changes in health care for people in the Eastern Mediterranean Region? Adham Ismail1 1Officer-in-Charge, WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean, Cairo, Egypt. Keywords: health financing, financial protection, universal health coverage, multi-communicable disease elimination, health system resilience, health equity, Eastern Mediterranean Citation: Ismail A. After Regional Committee 73, what changes in health care for people in the Eastern Mediterranean Region? East Mediterr Health J. 2026;32(10):659–661. https://doi.org/10.26719/2026.32.10.659. Copyright © Authors 2026. EMHJ is an open-access journal. This paper is available under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO licence (CC BY 3.0 IGO; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/igo). Meeting in Cairo from 13 to 15 October 2026 for the 73rd Session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Eastern Mediterranean (RC73), health ministers adopted 2 resolutions that could fundamentally change how countries finance health care and tackle communicable diseases across the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR). The scale of health needs stands in stark contrast to the resources available to meet them. The EMR is home to just 9% of the world’s population, yet almost half of all people requiring humanitarian assistance live here. The region accounts for less than 2% of the global health spending (1). As of the end of June 2026, 48 disease outbreaks were active across 17 EMR countries and territories, including cholera, measles, dengue, malaria, and vaccine-derived poliovirus (1). Between July 2025 and June 2026, some 632 attacks on health care were recorded, causing 1531 deaths – 86% of all such deaths worldwide (1). Meanwhile, 2 of 3 people in the region cannot obtain the care they need, and 1 in 5 cuts spending on food or education to pay for health care (1). The first resolution (EM/RC73/R.3) tackles inadequate financial protection that pushes millions of people into hardship when they seek care. The second (EM/ RC73/R.4) seeks to replace the fragmented approaches to disease elimination, which leave millions vulnerable to preventable illness and death. Both resolutions demand changes to how countries invest in health, organize services and use available resources. None of the resolutions can stop a war or end a humanitarian crisis, but both can change what happens when someone needs medical care: whether treatment pushes a family into poverty, or an infection is detected before it spreads, or health system protects those most at- risk. This is what makes implementation very important. Protecting people from the cost of care No family should have to choose between treating an illness and keeping a roof over its head. However, across the EMR, around 28% of people experience financial hardship due to health spending, and nearly 4 in 5 of those affected must forgo basic needs to obtain care (3). These are not simply financing problems. They are failures of financial protection, with consequences for health, household welfare and economic security. Governments fund only 48% of current health care expenditure, against 53% globally, and in the region’s low-income countries households pay 61% of health care costs out of pocket (3). At the same time, inefficient spending compounds the problem. WHO estimates that 20–40% of health spending is lost to inefficiency, through fragmented financing pools, inadequate regulation of the private sector, poorly designed payment systems, and overreliance on hospitals (3). Countries must therefore spend more on health, but they must also spend better. Resolution EM/RC73/R.3 calls for increased public financing, more equitable prepayment and pooling arrangements, strategic purchasing, closer links between health financing and social protection, and financing systems that can respond to crises, including through Islamic social financing (4). There is already progress to build on. Egypt is implementing universal health insurance, Pakistan is expanding its Sehat Sahulat Programme, Lebanon is using health taxes to create fiscal space, and Sudan is pooling procurement of high-cost medicines. Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are extending mandatory health insurance for their large expatriate populations (3). However, isolated reforms will not deliver Universal Health Coverage. Ministries of health and ministries of finance must work together to develop costed strategies backed by medium-term budgets, with greater investment in primary health care and financial protection for all. WHO will support these efforts through the regional Health Financing Taskforce (4). Disease elimination requires integration The case for a more integrated approach to communicable diseases is equally compelling. In 2023, communicable diseases accounted for more than 8 million disability- adjusted life years in the EMR, and the burden of some diseases is increasing (5). Nearly 28 million people live with chronic hepatitis B or C (6) and an estimated 78 million people still require interventions against neglected tropical diseases in the region (7). Malaria incidence more than doubled between 2015 and 2024, from 9.0 to 19.1 cases per 1000 population (5). And only 660 Editorial EMHJ – Vol. 32 No. 10 – 2026 28% of the 610 000 people living with HIV receive treatment (5). Many EMR countries continue to tackle individual diseases through separate programmes, each with its own surveillance, laboratory, procurement, and reporting systems. These arrangements duplicate efforts, stretch scarce resources and miss opportunities to reach people with multiple health needs. Resolution EM/RC73/R.2 seeks to change this by advancing an integrated approach to eliminating 14 priority communicable diseases. It calls for shared surveillance, diagnostics, procurement, and primary health care delivery, while preserving the specialised expertise needed to tackle individual diseases (5,8). Integration does not mean abandoning disease- specific programmes; it means making them work together. There is evidence that this approach delivers results. Oman eliminated mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis in 2022 through integrated maternal and child health services. And every US$ 1 invested in integrated neglected tropical disease interventions is estimated to generate around US$ 25 in returns (5). Integration and collaboration must extend beyond national borders. The 2022 devastating floods in Pakistan contributed to an estimated 6.6 million additional malaria cases and were linked to renewed local transmission in Islamic Republic of Iran (5). Along the Red Sea rim, Djibouti, Somalia, Sudan, and Yemen face overlapping disease threats that demand stronger cross-border cooperation (5). WHO will support countries through a regional implementation framework, measurable milestones and an investment case for integrated elimination (5,8). The challenge now is to translate these commitments into coordinated action at country level. Gains under pressure The EMR has demonstrated that sustained investment and coordinated action can deliver major public health gains. Nine countries have eliminated trachoma as a public health problem; most recently Egypt, Libya and Tunisia (5). Even in conflict-affected Sudan, coverage with the third dose of pentavalent vaccine increased from 38% in 2024 to 71% in 2025 (1). However, these achievements are fragile. In 2025, 2.4 million children in the EMR received no routine vaccines, an improvement on the 2024 achievement, but above the 2.1 million recorded in 2019 (9). Wild poliovirus transmission in Afghanistan and Pakistan has declined since peaking in 2024, but it persists in Karachi, southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and southern Afghanistan. Reaching every missed child during the coming low-transmission season will be critical to interrupting the remaining chains of transmission (9,10). These challenges are unfolding as resources become increasingly constrained. WHO’s base programme budget for the region was reduced by 14% for 2026–2027 (11), and the regional office has cut more than 300 staff positions (1). As of the end of June 2026, more than 40% of WHO’s emergency response requirements for the EMR remained unfunded (1). Countries must make better use of available resources, but efficiency cannot substitute for adequate, predictable financing, particularly in settings affected by conflict and displacement. International partners must also align their support with national priorities, strengthen country systems and channel their funding through national budgets wherever possible (3). Questions Regional Committee 74 should answer When the Regional Committee meets for its 74th Session in October 2027, household data would not have shown the impact of these decisions: the latest regional estimates of financial hardship are for 2022 (3). The test would be the earlier signals. Have ministries of finance backed costed health financing strategies in their budgets? Are countries rolling out integrated multi- disease elimination plans that target people previously missed, including those displaced across borders? Has the low-transmission season cut wild poliovirus circulation in its last reservoirs? If we cannot answer yes within a year, we would have mistaken agreement for progress. By RC74, countries must be able to demonstrate that these decisions are beginning to change how health care is financed, how services are delivered and, ultimately, what happens to people when they need health care. papers.title: Human Capital Development and Economic Growth in Nigeria: An Application of Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) Model Approach
papers.abstract: This study examined the impact of human capital development on economic growth in Nigeria from 1990 to 2020. The study adopted an ex post facto research design, to make an empirical investigation on the impact of human capital development proxy by Immunization against measles, infant mortality rate, and government expenditure on health and education as well as total energy consumption and on economic growth proxy by the growth rate of GDP. The study employed the ADF unit root test; the bounds test approach to cointegration, ARDL long and Short-run estimations as well as some post-estimation tests. Accordingly, the unit root test result showed that the variables under consideration are integrated at different orders 1 and 0. The bound test confirmed the presence of a long-run relationship among the variables under discourse. The ARDL estimation in the long run showed that a 1% decrease in infant mortality resulted in a 0.91% increase in GDPG. Also, a 1% increase in government expenditure on education and health increased GDPG by 0.23% and 0.05% respectively. The study recommended the prioritization of investment in education and healthcare to reduce infant mortality rates.
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

papers.title: A multi-region discrete time chain binomial model for infectious disease transmission
papers.abstract: Conventional mathematical models of infectious diseases often overlook the spatial spread of the disease, focusing only on local transmission. However, spatial propagation of various diseases has been observed mainly due to the movement of infectious individuals from one region to another. In this work, we propose a multiregion discrete-time chain binomial framework to model dependencies between infection time series from neighboring regions. The proposed model is based on the epidemiological principle that new infections arise from interactions between susceptible and previously infected individuals. To strengthen the statistical formulation, the probability of new infections within each spatial unit is modeled through a link function, by allowing it to depend on lagged local incidence, inter-regional transmission effects, and region-specific covariates. The framework also allows for higher-order temporal dependence through an AR(p) specification. To reduce complexity of the model as the number of regions increases, sparsity is imposed by using spatial contiguity matrices and k-nearest-neighbor structures. For estimating these multiregion models, an appropriate likelihood function maximization approach is proposed. A predictive likelihood based method is used to generate forecasts of disease counts in connected spatial units. In-depth analyses of two real measles datasets and simulation studies incorporating seasonal patterns, different weight matrices across connected regions, and varying intervention strategies are used to motivate the proposed modeling framework and demonstrate its ability to reproduce realistic outbreak dynamics. While the simulation studies demonstrate applicability of the general AR(p) approach, the real data analysis of measles shows that an AR(1) model is adequate to capture the temporal dependence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传统的传染病数学模型常常忽视疾病的空间传播,只关注局部的传播。然而,已观察到各种疾病的空间传播主要是由于感染者从一个地区移动到另一地区。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项工作中,我们提出了一个多区域离散时间链二项式框架来模拟相邻区域感染时间序列之间的依赖关系。
elements_zh.methods: 所提出的模型基于流行病学原理,即新的感染是由易感者和先前感染者之间的相互作用引起的。为了加强统计公式,每个空间单元内新感染的概率通过链接函数进行建模,允许其依赖于滞后的局部 发病率、区域间 传播 效应和区域特定的协变量。为了随着区域数量的增加而降低模型的复杂性,通过使用空间邻接矩阵和 k 最近邻结构来施加稀疏性。为了估计这些多区域模型,提出了一种适当的似然函数最大化方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 对两个真实 麻疹 数据集的深入分析和结合季节性模式、连接区域的不同权重矩阵以及不同干预策略的模拟研究用于激发所提出的建模框架,并证明其再现真实 麻疹 动态的能力。虽然模拟研究证明了一般 AR(p) 方法的适用性,但 麻疹 的实际数据分析表明 AR(1) 模型足以捕获时间依赖性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该框架允许通过 AR(p) 规范实现高阶时间依赖性,并通过使用稀疏性随着区域数量的增加而降低模型的复杂性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架可以重现真实的 暴发 动态,可用于预测连接空间单元中的疾病计数。这对于理解和预测 麻疹 在不同地区的传播尤其重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提出的模型依赖于这样的假设:新的感染是由易感者和先前感染者之间的相互作用引起的。麻疹 的真实数据分析表明,AR(1) 模型足以捕获时间依赖性,但该模型的性能可能会受到现实世界 传播 动力学的复杂性的限制。

analysis_zh.main_results: 对两个真实 麻疹 数据集的深入分析和结合季节性模式、连接区域的不同权重矩阵以及不同干预策略的模拟研究用于激发所提出的建模框架,并证明其再现真实 麻疹 动态的能力。虽然模拟研究证明了一般 AR(p) 方法的适用性,但 麻疹 的实际数据分析表明 AR(1) 模型足以捕获时间依赖性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该框架允许通过 AR(p) 规范实现高阶时间依赖性,并通过使用稀疏性随着区域数量的增加而降低模型的复杂性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架可以重现真实的 暴发 动态,可用于预测连接空间单元中的疾病计数。这对于理解和预测 麻疹 在不同地区的传播尤其重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提出的模型依赖于这样的假设:新的感染是由易感者和先前感染者之间的相互作用引起的。麻疹 的真实数据分析表明,AR(1) 模型足以捕获时间依赖性,但该模型的性能可能会受到现实世界 传播 动力学的复杂性的限制。

news.content: Key Takeaways The MMR vaccine is highly effective against measles. One dose provides 93% protection, while two doses provide 97% protection. Most people who receive both doses are protected for life. One dose provides 93% protection, while two doses provide 97% protection. Most people who receive both doses are protected for life. Some children may need the measles vaccine earlier than usual. Infants ages 6 to 11 months may need an early dose if traveling internationally or visiting or living in an area experiencing a measles outbreak. if traveling internationally or visiting or living in an area experiencing a measles outbreak. Measles spreads easily through the air, even before symptoms appear. Watch for fever, cough, red eyes, and a spreading rash. If you suspect measles, call your healthcare provider before visiting a clinic to help prevent further spread. Measles cases are surging in 2025 and 2026, with over 5,000 documented cases in the United States this year. Most infections occur in unvaccinated individuals, but what about those who’ve been vaccinated? Here’s what you need to know about MMR vaccine effectiveness, symptoms to watch for, and how to keep your children and family safe.
