supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Preventable Systems Failures Driven by Supply Gaps Trigger Bangladesh Measles Resurgence by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Preventable Systems Failures Driven by Supply Gaps Trigger Bangladesh Measles Resurgence Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A perspective analysis published in Discover Public Health reports that Bangladesh has confronted its most severe measles outbreak in decades during 2026, documenting more than 50,500 suspected cases and at least 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths between mid-March and mid-May. The analysis, authored by Md. Abdus Salam, characterizes this widespread public health crisis not as an unavoidable biological occurrence, but as a preventable systems failure that reversed years of hard-won progress toward disease elimination. Historically recognized as an international benchmark for immunization programming in resource-constrained environments, the country experienced an erosion of protective herd immunity when systemic administrative disruptions, nationwide vaccine supply shortages, and prolonged intervals between supplemental vaccination campaigns converged to expose expanding cohorts of unprotected children. The historical trajectory of measles control in Bangladesh highlights the scale of the recent setback. In the early 2000s, measles persisted as a major cause of pediatric mortality across the country, with national coverage for the first dose of measles-containing vaccine stagnating at or below 75 percent and zero administrative districts reaching the 95 percent coverage threshold necessary to interrupt transmission. Sustained national investments in the Expanded Programme on Immunization, combined with integrated child health days, routine vitamin A distribution, and recurring nationwide supplementary immunization activities, gradually lifted first-dose administrative coverage from approximately 74 to 89 percent in 2000 to between 94 and 118 percent by 2016. In parallel, the introduction of a routine second measles-containing vaccine dose in 2012 expanded second-dose coverage from roughly one-third of eligible children to more than 90 percent by the mid-2010s, driving laboratory-confirmed measles incidence down by more than 80 percent from approximately 40 cases per million population to 6 per million. Despite these extensive historical gains, national surveillance data compiled by domestic health agencies and international monitoring bodies revealed an underlying accumulation of susceptible individuals starting after 2019. National coverage estimates for both the first and second doses of the combined measles-rubella vaccine plateaued and subsequently exhibited modest declines. First-dose coverage slipped from approximately 88 to 89 percent down to 86 percent, while second-dose coverage dropped from roughly 89 percent to 80.7 percent by the 2023 to 2024 monitoring period, leaving an estimated 20 million children partially or entirely unprotected against infection. Compounding these gradual routine reductions, Bangladesh failed to conduct any nationwide measles-rubella supplementary immunization activities following its 2020 campaign, departing from its historical schedule of four-yearly catch-up exercises due to operational disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent domestic political instability. The vulnerability deepened considerably between 2024 and 2025 following a nationwide stockout of the measles-rubella vaccine, which the perspective links to procedural shifts in procurement arrangements and administrative delays that accompanied a broader political transition. A planned nationwide supplementary campaign originally scheduled for 2024 was postponed, remained unimplemented throughout 2025, and was ultimately cancelled altogether. While international evaluations by the World Health Organization and UNICEF recorded routine coverage figures of 97 percent for the first dose and 93 percent for the second dose in 2023, certain internal national reports cited an acute drop to approximately 56 to 59 percent coverage by 2025. Although the author notes that discrepancies between administrative datasets and independent field surveys preclude an absolute causal determination, the accumulated evidence indicates that these procurement disruptions expanded the pool of susceptible hosts precisely when routine delivery systems were operating under strain. When transmission expanded rapidly in early 2026, the infectious pathogen exploited these accumulated immunity gaps with severe clinical consequences. The National International Health Regulations Focal Point formally notified the World Health Organization of an accelerating nationwide increase in measles cases on April 4, 2026. Directorate General of Health Services data recorded 50,500 suspected cases and 415 deaths by May 11, reflecting a crude reported death-to-suspected-case ratio of approximately 0.82 percent. Epidemiological tracking between April 22 and May 4 documented cumulative suspected cases surging from 27,164 to 41,793, laboratory-confirmed infections rising from 3,934 to 5,467, and reported deaths increasing from 190 to 311. Approximately 79 to 80 percent of all reported infections occurred among children under five years of age, with 66 percent concentrated in children under two years and roughly one-third occurring in infants younger than nine months who were not yet eligible for standard routine measles immunization. The spatial distribution of cases revealed severe localized burdens, with the outbreak reaching 58 of Bangladesh’s 64 administrative districts across all eight divisions while concentrating heavily within specific urban slums, peripheral settlements, and humanitarian zones. In the capital division of Dhaka alone, situation reports documented more than 18,000 to 19,000 cases, heavily clustering within densely populated informal settlements including Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon. Within these crowded urban environments, high population density, economic precarity, and geographic mobility presented substantial barriers to routine healthcare delivery. Outside municipal centers, field monitoring in Gopalganj identified zero-dose children among highly mobile floating families who had been bypassed by both standard clinic-based schedules and targeted door-to-door immunization initiatives. Humanitarian settings presented another critical vulnerability during the 2026 resurgence, particularly within the congested Rohingya refugee camps established across Cox’s Bazar. Transmission within the camp complex escalated from 19 suspected cases in January to 199 in February, reaching 76 suspected cases with 8 confirmed infections by March. By mid-May, diagnostic testing confirmed 60 cases alongside 239 suspected cases and 5 attributable deaths, expanding to a cumulative total of 595 suspected cases and 60 laboratory-confirmed cases by May 20. The extreme transmissibility of the measles virus within these humanitarian enclaves was exacerbated by constrained baseline access to clinical services, widespread dependence on external humanitarian assistance, high rates of background malnutrition, and persistent cohorts of completely unvaccinated zero-dose infants residing in close quarters. The perspective emphasizes that the clinical severity of the outbreak was compounded by frequent secondary complications, most notably acute pneumonia, persistent diarrhea, and severe metabolic wasting linked directly to pre-existing childhood undernutrition and vitamin A deficiencies. Surging patient volumes placed severe operational strain on secondary and tertiary clinical centers, with daily hospital admissions frequently surpassing 1,200 to 1,300 patients. This influx rapidly overwhelmed pediatric wards and exposed structural deficits in facility-based isolation units, available health personnel, and laboratory diagnostic reagents. Clinical observations indicated that severe disease and fatal outcomes remained heavily concentrated among under-vaccinated or unvaccinated young children, demonstrating how nutritional deficits and immunization lapses synergistically worsen pediatric outcomes during large-scale community transmission. Bangladesh’s domestic outbreak mirrors a broader post-pandemic deterioration of measles control observed internationally. According to World Health Organization global monitoring figures, 59 countries experienced large or disruptive measles outbreaks in 2024—nearly three times the total recorded in 2021—including several jurisdictions that had previously attained verified elimination status. Worldwide, estimated coverage for the first vaccine dose reached approximately 84 to 86 percent in 2024, with second-dose uptake estimated at 76 percent, leaving global coverage well beneath the 95 percent threshold necessary to maintain community herd protection. Regionally, concurrent case increases and localized outbreaks were documented across India, Nepal, Thailand, and the Maldives, prompting public health authorities in neighboring Myanmar to reinforce cross-border surveillance and clinical preparedness along its frontier to mitigate potential cross-border transmission. In response to the crisis, the Government of Bangladesh joined with international partners, including the World Health Organization, UNICEF, and Gavi, to mount an emergency response campaign starting on April 5, 2026. Initially deployed across 30 high-risk upazilas in 18 districts, the intervention expanded into four city corporations before rolling out nationwide on April 20, strategically lowering the eligibility age to six months to shield vulnerable infants. Responders distributed more than 20 million vaccine doses, trained over 26,000 frontline health workers, and integrated vitamin A supplementation into clinical case management. Although administrative tracking recorded more than 18.3 million children vaccinated by May 19—surpassing initial national targets—an independent assessment published by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies on May 5 reported national administrative coverage at only 60.57 percent, noting that multiple districts had reached fewer than half of their target populations while active transmission continued. Concluding his evaluation, Salam argues that the 2026 epidemic serves as a clear indicator of structural fragility in primary health systems, illustrating that high national coverage metrics often obscure dangerous localized pockets of susceptibility. Rebuilding long-term resilience will require immediate stabilization of the national vaccine pipeline through secured buffer inventories, independent supplier verification mechanisms, and statutory protections that isolate essential medicine procurement from administrative or political transitions. Over the longer horizon, the perspective calls for institutionalizing regular supplementary catch-up campaigns, modernizing disease surveillance with real-time laboratory reporting, and prioritizing micro-planning in urban informal settlements and humanitarian camps to ensure sustained protection for marginalized and zero-dose populations before explosive outbreaks can emerge. Subject of Research: Systemic and operational drivers of the 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh Article Title: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh 2026 undermines elimination gains and requires urgent policy action Article References: Salam, M. A. (2026). Measles resurgence in Bangladesh 2026 undermines elimination gains and requires urgent policy action. supplementary_news.content: SHELTON, CT / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / NanoViricides, Inc., a publicly traded company (NYSE American: NNVC ) (the “Company”), and a clinical stage, leading global pioneer in the development of broad-spectrum antivirals based on host-mimetic nanomedicine technology that viruses cannot escape, announces that it is advancing its Measles drug development program towards clinical trials. There have been three deaths in children due to Measles in the USA in the last ten days, one each in the states of New York, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin i . This condition should be unacceptable in the USA because there is already a drug against Measles that has shown effectiveness in a humanized animal model of Measles, that has gone through extensive studies including Phase I human safety study, and that is already in two Phase II clinical trials for other viral infections. This investigational drug is NV-387, a novel, revolutionary broad-spectrum, antiviral drug developed by the Company. This drug has completed a juvenile animal model study as well. NV-387 is not yet FDA-approved or commercially available for treating Measles or any other viral disease. However, we believe the drug NV-387 now has sufficient data available to enable use under the US FDA physician-initiated investigational new drug application mechanism that is designed for use of experimental drugs for specific severe cases of disease, such as Measles. The Company continues to develop this drug in the regulatory pathways. There were 5,164 confirmed Measles cases within the USA (excluding international visitors) as of November 5, 2026, reported in 47 jurisdictions, with 4% of these being breakthrough cases in vaccinated individuals, and remaining 96% in unvaccinated individuals. 562 (11%) of the cases were hospitalized, and 4 confirmed Measles-caused deaths were recorded. A few additional deaths in Measles cases that are under CDC review have also occurred. Majority of hospitalizations occurred in children under 5 years of age. Only 4 states, namely Arkansas, Hawaii, Mississippi, and Nevada have not reported a Measles case in 2026, according to the CDC ii . These data indicate that Measles in the USA is continuing to expand in 2026. At this point, loss of the Measles elimination status achieved by the USA in 2000 as the very first country to achieve this status would be merely symbolic, emphasizing that Measles is a globally endemic virus with a very high potential for creating a contagion. Vaccines, even though effective, are inadequate as the only response to such a disease as Measles, and drugs to treat Measles infections are sorely needed. Of note, the D8 genotype of the Measles virus dominates in 2026 US cases iii whereas the Measles vaccine is based on the A genotype. NV-387, the Company’s revolutionary clinical stage broad-spectrum antiviral drug is currently in a Phase II clinical trials as an oral treatment for the Ebola Bundibugyo virus epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The same drug, NV-387, formulated as the same oral gummies formulation is also in a Phase II clinical trial for the treatment of Mpox (Monkeypox) in DRC in a different province. This very same drug has demonstrated remarkable antiviral activity against the Measles virus in a humanized hCD150+, IfnAR-/- mouse model of Measles virus infection and disease. The Company has also completed a repeat-dose juvenile mouse model toxicity study in which 4-day old mouse pups were dosed with repeated doses of NV-387 oral gummies formulation to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the drug and drug product in the context of the use of the drug in children. Under the conditions of this Juvenile Mouse Model study, the No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) was determined to be 1,230 mg/kg per dose administered three times daily, or 3,690 mg/kg/day, or a total cumulative drug exposure of 44,280 mg/kg over the 12 day dosing period. This was actually the highest dose level tested. Therefore, a Maximum Tolerable Dose (MTD) could not be estimated iv . Further, there was no mortality, systemic toxicity, treatment-related clinical observations, adverse effects on body weight gain, alterations in cardiovascular parameters, changes in clinical pathology, or treatment-related gross or microscopic pathological findings observed in either sex. According to established guidelines for juvenile animal model data extrapolation, a drug evaluated for safety toxicology in 4 day mouse pups supports clinical pediatric study in infants as young as 1 month v , under an appropriate regulatory study. Cases of Measles have been rising globally for different reasons. The measles outbreak in Bangladesh has continued to proliferate, claiming 24,073 lab-confirmed cases with 105 fatalities in lab-confirmed cases from 15 March to 10 November, 2026. During this period, a total of 207,428 patients with suspected measles were hospitalized and 1,263 persons, mostly children, have died of suspected measles, while 1,318 new suspected measles cases with at least 6 more child deaths were reported in just the last 24 hours in Bangladesh vi . The measles outbreak in Bangladesh has continued despite aggressive vaccination campaign that was undertaken since April-May 2026. There is currently no approved drug for measles. Vaccine does not help a patient already infected with the measles virus. Vaccinating already measles-exposed persons to avoid disease spread is attempted yet measles has continued to spread in the USA. Thus an effective treatment for Measles is an unmet medical need. NV-387 is the only drug candidate to our knowledge that has demonstrated strong in vivo activity against lethal infection with the Measles virus in a humanized animal model study, supporting its clinical regulatory development for treatment of Measles. NanoViricides is currently developing a Phase II clinical trial protocol for evaluating NV-387 as a treatment for measles. A draft is being circulated. The Company intends to bring this protocol under the purview of the US FDA in an IND process. Therefore, this work is expected to take some time. NV-387 has been granted a “Rare Pediatric Disease Drug” (RPDD) Designation by the US FDA Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD). This RPDD designation enables that a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) can be issued to the Company upon a successful Marketing Application (i.e. New Drug Application) for the use of NV-387 as a treatment for Measles, provided all of the required conditions are met. The Company can use the PRV, if granted, to reduce review times on another of its drug applications. A PRV can be sold to another Pharma Company for accelerating their drug program as well, which provides a high value to the purchaser. PRVs have been sold for as much as $200 Million vii . “The Rare Pediatric Disease Drug Designation and associated Priority Review Voucher that can be issued make a strong business case for development of NV-387 as a drug for the treatment of Measles,” said Anil R. Diwan, PhD., adding, “NV-387, as an effective drug would be an important tool to fight Measles resurgence in the USA and worldwide, when approved.” FDA has granted both ODD and RPDD for NV-387 as a Treatment of Measles. In addition to the PRV eligibility provided by the RPDD for NV-387 as a treatment of Measles, the Orphan Drug Designation qualifies NanoViricides for incentives including: Tax credits for qualified clinical trials; Exemption from certain user fees; Potential seven years of market exclusivity after approval; according to the US FDA viii . Measles continues to be a rare disease in the USA, with annual incidence rates well below 200,000 cases. Measles primarily affects children. These facts have qualified NV-387 for Measles Treatment for an Orphan Drug Designation, and also for a Rare Pediatric Disease Drug Designation. In a rare disease scenario, commercial revenue from the drug may be slow and small. The PRV is designed to incentivize drug development for rare pediatric diseases by providing additional business value. Measles cases are rising across the Western world including several European countries and the UK, as well as the USA and Canada. Additionally Mexico and several other Central and South American countries have also been suffering from rising Measles outbreaks. Measles is endemic globally; many countries that had achieved an elimination status for Measles have by now lost this status, due to severe outbreaks over the last three years ix . Measles is a highly contagious disease, and spreads via virus particles in bodily fluids upon close contact. A population vaccination rate of at least 95% is required to provide “herd immunity” and block community spread. Such a high rate is difficult to maintain for several reasons. Firstly, vaccine hesitancy is rising globally. Secondly, persons with co-morbidities such as immune-compromise status, diabetes, obesity, etc. do not respond fully to any vaccination. Even if vaccinated, such a person can still get Measles, suffering from possibly a mild disease, but will still be contagious and spread Measles. Additionally, the Measles virus continues to change, with the B and D genotypes in circulation currently, while the vaccines in use are still the ones developed for the A genotype in the 1960’s. Further, very high rates of infections in vaccinated subjects (called “breakthrough cases”), from 14% to 57%, have occurred in some outbreaks x suggesting that resistant virus strains may have been involved. Therefore, an effective treatment for Measles is an unmet medical need, that is expected to become even more important in the near future than it is today. Only an effective treatment can help the patient and can avoid the potential severe disease scenarios such as encephalitis, neurological disabilities, and potential fatalities as well as immune amnesia that can result from severe disease. Quicker recovery of a patient means less chances for spread and thus better ability to control an outbreak. This would require an effective treatment. NV-387 is an extremely broad-spectrum antiviral drug that has demonstrated strong effectiveness in relevant animal models of multiple human viral infections. These include RSV, COVID, Influenza, Mpox, Smallpox, and Measles. ABOUT NANOVIRICIDES NanoViricides, Inc. (the “Company”) ( www.nanoviricides.com ) is a publicly traded (NYSE-American, stock symbol NNVC) clinical stage company that is creating special purpose nanomaterials for antiviral therapy. The Company’s novel nanoviricide TM class of drug candidates and the nanoviricide TM technology are based on intellectual property, technology and proprietary know-how of TheraCour Pharma, Inc. The Company has a Memorandum of Understanding with TheraCour for the development of drugs based on these technologies for all antiviral infections. The MoU does not include cancer and similar diseases that may have viral origin but require different kinds of treatments. The Company has obtained broad, exclusive, sub-licensable, field licenses to drugs developed in several licensed fields from TheraCour Pharma, Inc. The Company’s business model is based on licensing technology from TheraCour Pharma Inc. for specific application verticals of specific viruses, as established at its foundation in 2005. Our lead drug candidate is NV-387, a broad-spectrum antiviral drug that we plan to develop as a treatment of RSV, COVID, Long COVID, Influenza, and other respiratory viral infections, as well as MPOX/Smallpox infections. Our other advanced drug candidate is NV-HHV-1 for the treatment of Shingles. The Company cannot project an exact date for filing an IND for any of its drugs because of dependence on a number of external collaborators and consultants. The Company is currently focused on advancing NV-387 into Phase II human clinical trials. The Company is also developing drugs against a number of viral diseases including oral and genital Herpes, viral diseases of the eye including EKC and herpes keratitis, H1N1 swine flu, H5N1 bird flu, seasonal Influenza, HIV, Hepatitis C, Rabies, Dengue fever, and Ebola virus, among others. NanoViricides’ platform technology and programs are based on the TheraCour ® nanomedicine technology of TheraCour, which TheraCour licenses from AllExcel. NanoViricides holds a worldwide exclusive perpetual license to this technology for several drugs with specific targeting mechanisms in perpetuity for the treatment of the following human viral diseases: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV/AIDS), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), Rabies, Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1 and HSV-2), Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV), Influenza and Asian Bird Flu Virus, Dengue viruses, Japanese Encephalitis virus, West Nile Virus, Ebola/Marburg viruses, and certain Coronaviruses. The Company intends to obtain a license for RSV, Poxviruses, and/or Enteroviruses if the initial research is successful. As is customary, the Company must state the risk factor that the path to typical drug development of any pharmaceutical product is extremely lengthy and requires substantial capital. As with any drug development efforts by any company, there can be no assurance at this time that any of the Company’s pharmaceutical candidates would show sufficient effectiveness and safety for human clinical development. Further, there can be no assurance at this time that successful results against coronavirus in our lab will lead to successful clinical trials or a successful pharmaceutical product. This press release contains forward-looking statements that reflect the Company’s current expectation regarding future events. Actual events could differ materially and substantially from those projected herein and depend on a number of factors. Certain statements in this release, and other written or oral statements made by NanoViricides, Inc. are “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. You should not place undue reliance on forward-looking statements since they involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors which are, in some cases, beyond the Company’s control and which could, and likely will, materially affect actual results, levels of activity, performance or achievements. The Company assumes no obligation to publicly update or revise these forward-looking statements for any reason, or to update the reasons actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements, even if new information becomes available in the future. Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from the company’s expectations include, but are not limited to, those factors that are disclosed under the heading “Risk Factors” and elsewhere in documents filed by the company from time to time with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission and other regulatory authorities. Although it is not possible to predict or identify all such factors, they may include the following: demonstration and proof of principle in preclinical trials that a nanoviricide is safe and effective; successful development of our product candidates; our ability to seek and obtain regulatory approvals, including with respect to the indications we are seeking; the successful commercialization of our product candidates; and market acceptance of our products. supplementary_news.title: The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status, Data Suggests
supplementary_news.excerpt: A panel of scientific experts will convene on Tuesday to evaluate the United States’ measles elimination status. But genetic data already shows the virus is once again endemic.

supplementary_news.content_title: The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status, Data Suggests
supplementary_news.content: Supported by The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status, Data Suggests An international panel of scientific experts will convene on Tuesday to evaluate the status, but genetic data already shows the virus is once again entrenched in the United States. Measles is once again endemic — a constant and predictable presence — in the United States, 26 years after it was declared eliminated in the country, an analysis of genetic data from outbreaks of the disease has found. Data from the outbreaks will be the focus of deliberations by an international panel of scientific experts convening on Tuesday to decide whether the United States should lose its official designation as a nation that has eliminated measles. An announcement of the decision is expected on Nov. 17. The New York Times asked several scientists to analyze the publicly available genetic data before the meeting. Achieving elimination status in 2000 was a hard-fought public health victory for the United States. But with skepticism about the safety of vaccines growing in recent years, outbreaks have become more frequent. Over the past two years, cases have soared, with nearly 5,200 reported so far this year. Last week alone, Pennsylvania, New York and Wisconsin each reported a death associated with measles, bringing this year’s total to eight, more than the combined deaths from 2000 through 2024. To officially lose elimination status, a committee of the Pan American Health Organization, a branch of the World Health Organization, must determine that the country has had uninterrupted transmission of measles for more than 12 months. Publicly available data shows that several chains of transmission have continued for more than a year in the United States, according to scientists who analyzed the data at the request of The New York Times. supplementary_news.content_title: An Investigational Drug to Tackle Measles Outbreaks
supplementary_news.content: SHELTON, CT / ACCESS Newswire / November 10, 2026 / NanoViricides, Inc., a publicly traded company (NYSE American: NNVC ) (the “Company”), and a clinical stage, leading global pioneer in the development of broad-spectrum antivirals based on host-mimetic nanomedicine technology that viruses cannot escape, announces that it is advancing its Measles drug development program towards clinical trials. There have been three deaths in children due to Measles in the USA in the last ten days, one each in the states of New York, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin i . This condition should be unacceptable in the USA because there is already a drug against Measles that has shown effectiveness in a humanized animal model of Measles, that has gone through extensive studies including Phase I human safety study, and that is already in two Phase II clinical trials for other viral infections. This investigational drug is NV-387, a novel, revolutionary broad-spectrum, antiviral drug developed by the Company. This drug has completed a juvenile animal model study as well. NV-387 is not yet FDA-approved or commercially available for treating Measles or any other viral disease. However, we believe the drug NV-387 now has sufficient data available to enable use under the US FDA physician-initiated investigational new drug application mechanism that is designed for use of experimental drugs for specific severe cases of disease, such as Measles. The Company continues to develop this drug in the regulatory pathways. There were 5,164 confirmed Measles cases within the USA (excluding international visitors) as of November 5, 2026, reported in 47 jurisdictions, with 4% of these being breakthrough cases in vaccinated individuals, and remaining 96% in unvaccinated individuals. 562 (11%) of the cases were hospitalized, and 4 confirmed Measles-caused deaths were recorded. A few additional deaths in Measles cases that are under CDC review have also occurred. Majority of hospitalizations occurred in children under 5 years of age. Only 4 states, namely Arkansas, Hawaii, Mississippi, and Nevada have not reported a Measles case in 2026, according to the CDC ii . These data indicate that Measles in the USA is continuing to expand in 2026. At this point, loss of the Measles elimination status achieved by the USA in 2000 as the very first country to achieve this status would be merely symbolic, emphasizing that Measles is a globally endemic virus with a very high potential for creating a contagion. Vaccines, even though effective, are inadequate as the only response to such a disease as Measles, and drugs to treat Measles infections are sorely needed. Of note, the D8 genotype of the Measles virus dominates in 2026 US cases iii whereas the Measles vaccine is based on the A genotype. NV-387, the Company’s revolutionary clinical stage broad-spectrum antiviral drug is currently in a Phase II clinical trials as an oral treatment for the Ebola Bundibugyo virus epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The same drug, NV-387, formulated as the same oral gummies formulation is also in a Phase II clinical trial for the treatment of Mpox (Monkeypox) in DRC in a different province. This very same drug has demonstrated remarkable antiviral activity against the Measles virus in a humanized hCD150+, IfnAR-/- mouse model of Measles virus infection and disease. The Company has also completed a repeat-dose juvenile mouse model toxicity study in which 4-day old mouse pups were dosed with repeated doses of NV-387 oral gummies formulation to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the drug and drug product in the context of the use of the drug in children. Under the conditions of this Juvenile Mouse Model study, the No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) was determined to be 1,230 mg/kg per dose administered three times daily, or 3,690 mg/kg/day, or a total cumulative drug exposure of 44,280 mg/kg over the 12 day dosing period. This was actually the highest dose level tested. Therefore, a Maximum Tolerable Dose (MTD) could not be estimated iv . Further, there was no mortality, systemic toxicity, treatment-related clinical observations, adverse effects on body weight gain, alterations in cardiovascular parameters, changes in clinical pathology, or treatment-related gross or microscopic pathological findings observed in either sex. According to established guidelines for juvenile animal model data extrapolation, a drug evaluated for safety toxicology in 4 day mouse pups supports clinical pediatric study in infants as young as 1 month v , under an appropriate regulatory study. Cases of Measles have been rising globally for different reasons. The measles outbreak in Bangladesh has continued to proliferate, claiming 24,073 lab-confirmed cases with 105 fatalities in lab-confirmed cases from 15 March to 10 November, 2026. During this period, a total of 207,428 patients with suspected measles were hospitalized and 1,263 persons, mostly children, have died of suspected measles, while 1,318 new suspected measles cases with at least 6 more child deaths were reported in just the last 24 hours in Bangladesh vi . The measles outbreak in Bangladesh has continued despite aggressive vaccination campaign that was undertaken since April-May 2026. There is currently no approved drug for measles. Vaccine does not help a patient already infected with the measles virus. Vaccinating already measles-exposed persons to avoid disease spread is attempted yet measles has continued to spread in the USA. Thus an effective treatment for Measles is an unmet medical need. NV-387 is the only drug candidate to our knowledge that has demonstrated strong in vivo activity against lethal infection with the Measles virus in a humanized animal model study, supporting its clinical regulatory development for treatment of Measles. NanoViricides is currently developing a Phase II clinical trial protocol for evaluating NV-387 as a treatment for measles. A draft is being circulated. The Company intends to bring this protocol under the purview of the US FDA in an IND process. Therefore, this work is expected to take some time. NV-387 has been granted a “Rare Pediatric Disease Drug” (RPDD) Designation by the US FDA Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD). This RPDD designation enables that a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) can be issued to the Company upon a successful Marketing Application (i.e. New Drug Application) for the use of NV-387 as a treatment for Measles, provided all of the required conditions are met. The Company can use the PRV, if granted, to reduce review times on another of its drug applications. A PRV can be sold to another Pharma Company for accelerating their drug program as well, which provides a high value to the purchaser. PRVs have been sold for as much as $200 Million vii . “The Rare Pediatric Disease Drug Designation and associated Priority Review Voucher that can be issued make a strong business case for development of NV-387 as a drug for the treatment of Measles,” said Anil R. Diwan, PhD., adding, “NV-387, as an effective drug would be an important tool to fight Measles resurgence in the USA and worldwide, when approved.” FDA has granted both ODD and RPDD for NV-387 as a Treatment of Measles. In addition to the PRV eligibility provided by the RPDD for NV-387 as a treatment of Measles, the Orphan Drug Designation qualifies NanoViricides for incentives including: Tax credits for qualified clinical trials; Exemption from certain user fees; Potential seven years of market exclusivity after approval; according to the US FDA viii . Measles continues to be a rare disease in the USA, with annual incidence rates well below 200,000 cases. Measles primarily affects children. These facts have qualified NV-387 for Measles Treatment for an Orphan Drug Designation, and also for a Rare Pediatric Disease Drug Designation. In a rare disease scenario, commercial revenue from the drug may be slow and small. The PRV is designed to incentivize drug development for rare pediatric diseases by providing additional business value. Measles cases are rising across the Western world including several European countries and the UK, as well as the USA and Canada. Additionally Mexico and several other Central and South American countries have also been suffering from rising Measles outbreaks. Measles is endemic globally; many countries that had achieved an elimination status for Measles have by now lost this status, due to severe outbreaks over the last three years ix . Measles is a highly contagious disease, and spreads via virus particles in bodily fluids upon close contact. A population vaccination rate of at least 95% is required to provide “herd immunity” and block community spread. Such a high rate is difficult to maintain for several reasons. Firstly, vaccine hesitancy is rising globally. Secondly, persons with co-morbidities such as immune-compromise status, diabetes, obesity, etc. do not respond fully to any vaccination. Even if vaccinated, such a person can still get Measles, suffering from possibly a mild disease, but will still be contagious and spread Measles. Additionally, the Measles virus continues to change, with the B and D genotypes in circulation currently, while the vaccines in use are still the ones developed for the A genotype in the 1960’s. Further, very high rates of infections in vaccinated subjects (called “breakthrough cases”), from 14% to 57%, have occurred in some outbreaks x suggesting that resistant virus strains may have been involved. Therefore, an effective treatment for Measles is an unmet medical need, that is expected to become even more important in the near future than it is today. Only an effective treatment can help the patient and can avoid the potential severe disease scenarios such as encephalitis, neurological disabilities, and potential fatalities as well as immune amnesia that can result from severe disease. Quicker recovery of a patient means less chances for spread and thus better ability to control an outbreak. This would require an effective treatment. NV-387 is an extremely broad-spectrum antiviral drug that has demonstrated strong effectiveness in relevant animal models of multiple human viral infections. These include RSV, COVID, Influenza, Mpox, Smallpox, and Measles. ABOUT NANOVIRICIDES NanoViricides, Inc. (the “Company”) ( www.nanoviricides.com ) is a publicly traded (NYSE-American, stock symbol NNVC) clinical stage company that is creating special purpose nanomaterials for antiviral therapy. The Company’s novel nanoviricide TM class of drug candidates and the nanoviricide TM technology are based on intellectual property, technology and proprietary know-how of TheraCour Pharma, Inc. The Company has a Memorandum of Understanding with TheraCour for the development of drugs based on these technologies for all antiviral infections. The MoU does not include cancer and similar diseases that may have viral origin but require different kinds of treatments. The Company has obtained broad, exclusive, sub-licensable, field licenses to drugs developed in several licensed fields from TheraCour Pharma, Inc. The Company’s business model is based on licensing technology from TheraCour Pharma Inc. for specific application verticals of specific viruses, as established at its foundation in 2005. Our lead drug candidate is NV-387, a broad-spectrum antiviral drug that we plan to develop as a treatment of RSV, COVID, Long COVID, Influenza, and other respiratory viral infections, as well as MPOX/Smallpox infections. Our other advanced drug candidate is NV-HHV-1 for the treatment of Shingles. The Company cannot project an exact date for filing an IND for any of its drugs because of dependence on a number of external collaborators and consultants. The Company is currently focused on advancing NV-387 into Phase II human clinical trials. The Company is also developing drugs against a number of viral diseases including oral and genital Herpes, viral diseases of the eye including EKC and herpes keratitis, H1N1 swine flu, H5N1 bird flu, seasonal Influenza, HIV, Hepatitis C, Rabies, Dengue fever, and Ebola virus, among others. NanoViricides’ platform technology and programs are based on the TheraCour ® nanomedicine technology of TheraCour, which TheraCour licenses from AllExcel. NanoViricides holds a worldwide exclusive perpetual license to this technology for several drugs with specific targeting mechanisms in perpetuity for the treatment of the following human viral diseases: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV/AIDS), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), Rabies, Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1 and HSV-2), Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV), Influenza and Asian Bird Flu Virus, Dengue viruses, Japanese Encephalitis virus, West Nile Virus, Ebola/Marburg viruses, and certain Coronaviruses. The Company intends to obtain a license for RSV, Poxviruses, and/or Enteroviruses if the initial research is successful. As is customary, the Company must state the risk factor that the path to typical drug development of any pharmaceutical product is extremely lengthy and requires substantial capital. As with any drug development efforts by any company, there can be no assurance at this time that any of the Company’s pharmaceutical candidates would show sufficient effectiveness and safety for human clinical development. Further, there can be no assurance at this time that successful results against coronavirus in our lab will lead to successful clinical trials or a successful pharmaceutical product. supplementary_news.content: 24/7 LiveRaleighDurhamFayettevilleSurrounding Area 50° Measles What parents need to know as measles outbreaks spread across the US Eight people, including a Wisconsin infant, have died of measles this year. Watch ABC News live news stream and get 24/7 latest, breaking news coverage, and live video. ByYi-Jin Yu Tuesday, November 10, 2026 1:19PM Share Follow ABC11 on Google More measles cases are being reported across the U.S., and eight people have died so far, including an infant in Wisconsin, the first measles-related death in the state since 1990, according to health officials. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says there have been nearly 5,200 measles cases across 45 states and Washington, D.C., so far this year, as more have decided to opt out of vaccination. "I'm extremely concerned, and the reason for that is there's no indication that these outbreaks will be slowing down at this point," Dr. Andrew Handel, a pediatric infectious diseases physician at Stony Brook Children's Hospital in Stony Brook, New York, told ABC News. As the measles virus continues to spread, here's what parents should know about the disease. What is measles? Measles is a highly contagious virus that can cause acute respiratory illness, according to the CDC. It is more contagious that other respiratory viruses, such as the common cold, the flu or COVID. "It is the most contagious infection that we know of," Handel said. "The estimate is that for every person who has measles, they can infect up to 18 people who are unvaccinated with it." Measles is spread through the air when someone infected with the virus exhales or coughs. People can also become infected after breathing in contaminated air or by touching an infected surface and then touching their eyes, noses or mouths, the CDC states. "For measles, it spreads through airborne means, which means that once [an infected person breathes] it out, it actually stays circulating in the air for up to two hours after they leave that room," Handel explained. "If someone goes to their doctor to be checked for measles, and they don't recognize that they have measles, and then they walk out of the room, someone who comes in an hour and a half later can become infected with measles." What are the symptoms of measles? The CDC notes that measles can initially look like other respiratory infections, with symptoms including a cough, runny nose, conjunctivitis (red, watery eyes), or a high fever, which can increase to more than 104 degrees Fahrenheit. The most recognizable symptom of measles is a rash that typically starts at the head and moves down the body. "People break out into the rash, which starts as red, dark circles that usually start right at the hairline and work their way down the body," Handel said. "As it works its way down, you see the red circles, the red dots further down. But the place where it started -- so, on the face -- the redness will start to come together, so it'll look like a sheet of redness, and it, again, starts from the head and works its way down, which is very particular." Top Stories Let's salute our heroes: Events to honor North Carolina veterans and service members SS United States completes final voyage, sinks to Gulf floor to become artificial reef House tables Hegseth impeachment, effectively killing it in current Congress "We also see something called Koplik spots, which are usually whitish, bluish dots that can appear on the inside of the cheek," Handel added. "Those tend to come up a couple days before the rash, so it can help us to make the diagnosis a bit earlier." Measles symptoms typically begin seven to 14 days after initial contact with the virus, according to the CDC. What are the complications of measles? A common misconception about measles, as the CDC notes, is that infection with the virus isn't severe. The CDC and Handel both stress that measles infections can give rise to serious complications, from short-term issues like diarrhea and ear infections, to serious to life-threatening long-term problems and death. "Many children, many people can go on and have complications ... that can include severe pneumonias, dehydration, and also acute brain infections, where suddenly, you can have seizures," Handel said. He continued, "You can have changes in behavior. You can develop meningitis where there's neck pain and headache because the measles infection [has] infiltrated into the spinal fluid. There are some children who, especially if they're infected before they turn 1 year old, in particular, can develop a neurologic progressive disease [called subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, or SSPE,] that ultimately results in death up to 10 years later. And so, there are some really scary outcomes from it." How can measles be prevented? According to the CDC, the best way to protect against measles is with the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine, or MMR, which can be administered to children starting at 12 months old. Children who receive a first dose of the MMR vaccine then need to get a second dose when they are between 4 and 6 years old. "The only way to prevent infections when there is an ongoing national outbreak at levels that we haven't seen in decades is to get the MMR vaccine," Handel said. "It is safe, it is effective, and it's the best thing we can do again to stop this outbreak and get the country back to the rates of measles infections that we'd previously seen." Not everyone may be able to get an MMR vaccine, such as children with cancer, those who are pregnant, and people who have compromised immune systems, so it is important to discuss your children's and family's eligibility and concerns with a medical provider. Kennedy Jr.)對疫苗政策的態度。 甘迺迪長期對疫苗安全性提出質疑,上任後更大幅改組疫苗專家諮詢委員會,並宣布取消部分mRNA疫苗研發計畫的聯邦資助。他對疫苗政策的立場,以及政府接連調整公共衛生專業制度的做法,引發醫學界對美國防疫方向的疑慮。 路透社報導,今年美國麻疹病例中,有96%屬於未接種疫苗或接種狀態不明的人群。今年已經有562人因麻疹住院,佔確診病例約11%。麻疹並不是一般的發燒出疹疾病,嚴重時可能引發肺炎、腦炎,甚至死亡。 美國可能失去維持26年的防疫成果 1963年麻疹疫苗問世後,美國政府推動大規模接種,病例很快就大幅下降。到了1971年,麻疹、腮腺炎、德國麻疹三合一疫苗(MMR)推出,1989年美國進一步建議兒童接種第二劑疫苗。經過數十年的疫苗接種計畫,美國終於在2000年達成「消除麻疹」的目標。 然而,2025年1月德州西部首先爆發疫情,隨後蔓延至其他州,猶他州、亞利桑那州、南卡羅來納州及賓夕法尼亞州都出現大規模感染。 泛美衛生組織將於11月10日至13日召開閉門會議,由流行病學、公共衛生、病毒學、兒科及免疫學專家組成的獨立委員會,審查美國2025年及2026年上半年的疫情資料,包括病毒基因、傳播鏈、疫苗接種率及疫情監測能力。 這項判定並非單純計算病例數,也不是只要發現基因相同的病毒就能認定持續傳播,而是必須綜合流行病學與病毒學證據,確認相關病毒譜系是否存在連續至少12個月的本土傳播。 加拿大已在2025年因為麻疹持續傳播超過一年,失去消除地位,如今美國也面臨相同風險。 美國麻疹疫情擴大的同時,川普政府卻在2025年推動聯邦衛生機構大規模重組。 DOGE裁減CDC人力 邊境檢疫也受到衝擊 2025年3月,美國衛生與公共服務部(HHS)宣布,將透過重組與人力精簡,把原本約82,000名員工縮減至62,000名,部門數量也從28個整併為15個。官方公布的計畫包括CDC減少約2,400個職位、食品藥物管理局(FDA)減少約3,500人,以及國家衛生研究院(NIH)減少約1,200人。這些數字是當時公布的精簡規劃,並非全部已經實際裁撤的人數。 政府宣稱,裁減與整併是為了減少行政重複、節省支出,並讓衛生機構更加有效率。但問題在於,公共衛生機關並非一般行政部門,許多看似平時不需要大量人力的工作,恰恰是在疫情爆發時才顯現重要性。 美國NPR在2025年2月報導,CDC負責國際旅客檢疫的港口衛生站已經受到人力縮減影響。當時全美20個港口衛生站中,有3個沒有CDC派駐人員,另外一半沒有主管。 這些衛生站設於國際機場及陸路邊境,負責辨識旅客可能攜帶的傳染病,必要時協調地方衛生機關進行接觸者追蹤。它們也是美國防範境外傳染病輸入的重要防線。 NPR引述CDC內部人士表示,部分衛生站因為人力不足,不得不由其他據點支援,甚至放棄某些原本應該執行的工作。 此外,CDC內部負責疫情預測與分析、傳染病監測及現場應變的人員,也曾受到裁員波及。2025年10月,更有超過1,000名CDC員工收到裁員通知,其中包括部分負責麻疹疫情應變的人員。雖然政府後來撤回超過一半的裁員通知,保留部分疫情應變人員,但其他疾病監測及生物安全專業人員仍受到影響。 比起人力裁減,更具爭議的是衛生部長甘迺迪對疫苗政策及專業諮詢制度的改革。 甘迺迪長期對疫苗安全性提出質疑。2025年6月,他撤換原有的17名免疫實踐諮詢委員會(ACIP)成員。這個委員會長期負責審查疫苗安全性、有效性及接種必要性,並向CDC提供疫苗接種建議,是美國疫苗政策的重要專業諮詢機制。 小羅伯甘迺迪反對疫苗,改變疫苗政策方向 甘迺迪宣稱,此舉是為了重建民眾對疫苗的信任,但一次撤換全部原有委員,也引發醫學界對專業審議獨立性的疑慮。 2025年8月,甘迺迪又宣布終止或縮減生物醫學高級研究與發展管理局(BARDA)旗下22項mRNA疫苗研發計畫,涉及近5億美元資金,包括流感及新冠病毒疫苗等研究。他認為mRNA疫苗對上呼吸道感染的保護效果不足,應將資源轉向其他疫苗技術。不過,這項決定並非全面禁止mRNA技術,而是停止或縮減特定聯邦資助計畫。 2026年1月,川普政府進一步調整兒童疫苗接種建議,將原本普遍建議接種的疫苗項目從17種縮減為11種,部分疫苗改列為高風險族群接種或由醫師與家長共同決策。美國兒科學會等醫學團體對此提出法律挑戰,聯邦法院於3月16日暫時凍結相關政策變更及部分ACIP委員任命。 必須說明的是,麻疹、腮腺炎、德國麻疹三合一疫苗(MMR)並未被取消,美國CDC仍將其列為兒童常規疫苗。真正值得關注的,是政府高層對疫苗政策的態度、專家諮詢制度的改變,以及這些措施是否進一步動搖民眾對疫苗接種的信任。 喪失「巅疹消除國」地位的運作機制 美國是否失去麻疹消除地位,由泛美衛生組織(PAHO)負責認定。PAHO是世界衛生組織(WHO)的美洲區域辦事處,同時也是美洲區域的專門衛生機構。 PAHO設立了一個獨立專家機構,名為「麻疹、風疹及先天性風疹症候群消除區域監測與重新認證委員會」,每年至少召開一次會議,監測及審查美洲各國麻疹與風疹的消除情況。 本次會議將於11月10日至13日舉行,審查美國2025年及2026年上半年的疫情資料。專家委員會完成評估後,將向PAHO主任提出建議,再由主任正式通知相關國家的認定結果。 費城兒童醫院疫苗教育中心主任、傳染病科主治醫師保羅·奧菲特(Paul Offit)表示,即使美國失去麻疹消除地位,也應該將此視為重新投入防疫工作的警鐘。他向ABC新聞表示:「往好的方面看,失去消除傳染病的地位,可以成為重新動員的號召。但失去這項地位,將是一個巨大的損失。」 貝勒醫學院國家熱帶醫學院院長彼得·霍特茲(Peter Hotez)則認為,美國麻疹疫情已經重新擴散,是否能將各地疫情串連成同一條傳播鏈,並不是最重要的問題。 他表示:「麻疹已經捲土重來。在我看來,是否能將這些特定疫情串連起來,反而沒有那麼重要,真正重要的是,麻疹已經在美國不同地區廣泛傳播。」 文章來源:Upcoming meeting could determine if US loses its measles elimination status
